job.title: AWFC Academy Sports Scientist (Casual Role)
job.location: The Hive London, London, HA8 6AG, GB
job.html_description:
The Role

We are looking for an Academy Sports Scientist to work with us at AWFC on a casual basis.

In this exciting casual role, you'll deliver an effective interpretation of data collected via Global Positioning System (GPS) in a way that Coaches can interpret and understand. You'll play a crucial role in producing players who are durable, resilient from injury, and possess a level of physicality that enables them to express the technical and tactical skills required to transition to the Women's First Team.

You will be entrusted to develop ideas that can complement the AWFC long term athletic development model to progress the athleticism of players in our Academy, delivering information and guidance in relation to the maturational status of players through their growth.

Who we are

We are one of the most famous clubs in world football, with a rich heritage and history of success – read more about our history, here.

Beyond that, we are passionate about our local community and, behind the scenes, we have a wide variety of opportunities and career paths for all. We have a very defined purpose: to act for a winning team, culture and community. We achieve this by ensuring we are courageous in the pursuit of progress, we champion our community and each other, and that we do the right thing (even when no one is looking).

Discover why ‘Our Gunners’ are proud to be part of our team - view their stories here.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

We are committed to ensuring that our environments for children, young people and adults at risk remain safe and inclusive. We therefore require successful candidates to complete an enhanced DBS check and other essential background checks prior to starting their employment.

Your day-to-day

  • Leverage data to drive positive impact - you'll bridge the physical gap to our Women's First Team via data collection and interpretation, informing and adapting sessions, whilst working in line with our Women's Academy game model, and you will lead and oversee the GPS management on a day-to-day basis, including daily live data feedback and plotting future targets

  • Oversee player fitness profiling and growth - you will support and develop our Academy fitness profiling and ensure that it is age-specific, comprehensive and in line with FA requirements, and you'll develop an understanding of where players maturational status is, and how we can support them through all stages of their growth

  • Champion individual development - you'll implement an individual development approach, with regular touch points to review the previous block and constantly development our athletes as well as developing the team as a whole

  • Support the development of our Academy programme - you will attend reviews and contribute to reports with key stakeholders throughout the season, to have input into the development of our Women's Academy programme

  • Assist in the education of colleagues - you'll help Academy colleagues to understand the requirements of robustness and resilience amongst athletes, through the physical guidance of sessions

  • Create and implement sports science strategies - you will collaborate with our multidisciplinary team to optimise the squads' abilities to perform throughout the season, and you'll demonstrate the desire to develop the provision within the programme through education and learning strategies

  • Feed into talent ID processes - you'll support the development of talent ID profiles for age and position appropriate information to inform our decision-making process using data collection
     

What we are looking for

  • History of working with elite athletes - you're proud of your previous success of working with elite footballers and/or athletes domestically and internationally, and you have a natural enthusiasm for coaching and mentoring elite young and senior players

  • Credible expertise - you hold a degree level qualification (or equivalent) in Sports Science or Strength and Conditioning, as well as an FA Safeguarding Children Certificate

  • Experience working as a key part of a multidisciplinary team - you have a track record of operating within a multidisciplinary performance team and providing strength and conditioning, sports science, or physiotherapy services to elite players, to improve performance, prevent injuries and ensure timely recoveries

  • Background in Women's football - you have knowledge of the FA Girls' Talent Pathway and WSL Academy structure

  • Data competency - you are confident in using and interpreting GPS data, ideally in a football or sport context

  • Best-in-class communication skills - you're an effective communicator with the ability to build meaningful, impactful strategic relationships with colleagues and players

  • Organised and adaptable approach - you can demonstrate excellent session planning and organisational skills

  • Flexible and adaptable mindset - you possess a willingness to work weekends and can be flexible to the needs of an ever-changing schedule, and you are able to travel independently

Position of Trust - As someone in a position of trust role involving regular, direct contact with children or vulnerable adults you will be expected to uphold high standards of conduct to prevent abuse, including sexual, physical, or emotional harm. This role requires you to keep updated with both Club and FA Safeguarding training and education

Arsenal for Everyone

Arsenal for Everyone is our commitment to promoting and embracing equality, diversity and inclusion, so that everyone connected to the club feels like they belong to the same Arsenal family. We believe that diversity of background, skills and experience drives our success on and off the pitch. 


Disability Confident Leader

We are a Disability Confident Leader. We actively welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions. If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a ‘disabled person’ according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below. The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment decisions.

Application Closing Date - Wednesday 23rd September 2026

Please note: we reserve the right to close the position early if application volumes are particularly high. We encourage you to get your application in sooner rather than later.

Updates on the status of your application will be sent via email, please routinely check your spam and junk folders, as occasionally emails sent via the Teamtailor platform will find themselves there.

Good luck!

job.title: Casual Stadium Tour Photo Sales Host
job.html_description:
The Role

We are looking for motivated Photo Sales Hosts on a casual basis, who will be providing exceptional experiences for our supporters along our stadium tour route and museum.

You will capture photos, produce quality photos in photo books and subsequently sell those photo books to our guests whilst providing an exceptional customer service experience as the face of our club.

Rate of pay: London Living Wage.

Casual Roles

Working with our club on a Casual basis offers a flexible and short-term arrangement. Unlike full-time roles, shifts are scheduled based on both on our needs and your availability. These shifts may include matchdays, evenings, weekends, and events. 

View more about our Casual roles here.

Who we are

We are one of the most famous clubs in world football, with a rich heritage and history of success – read more about our history, here.

Beyond that, we are passionate about our local community and, behind the scenes, we have a wide variety of opportunities and career paths for all. We have a very defined purpose: to act for a winning team, culture and community. We achieve this by ensuring we are courageous in the pursuit of progress, we champion our community and each other, and that we do the right thing (even when no one is looking).

Discover why ‘Our Gunners’ are proud to be part of our team - view their stories here.

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

We are committed to ensuring that our environments for children, young people and adults at risk remain safe and inclusive. We therefore require successful candidates to complete a DBS check and other essential background checks prior to starting their employment. Depending on the responsibilities of the role, a DBS will be either a basic, standard, or enhanced check.

Your day-to-day

  • Shoot high quality photos - you will be skilled to shoot high quality photos by capturing every guest and ensuring they meet photo composition standards

  • Drive sales and upselling opportunities - you’ll actively sell and upsell products by engaging with customers in a confident, friendly way and recommending products that meet their needs

  • Print and pack photos - you will be enthused to deliver in a timely manner ensuring all photos are cut cleanly

  • Deliver excellent customer service - you'll confidently provide a world-class supporter experience through interacting in a proactive, friendly and enthusiastic manner

  • Champion our products - you will become an expert of all tour and photo products, areas of the stadium, and experiences

 

What we are looking for

  • Experience in a retail based role - you thrive when you're delivering amazing experiences at a visitor attraction or in a front line, customer facing role

  • Confident communicator - you've got a natural passion for providing an engaging service to all visitors in our stores

  • Passionate teamplayer - you pride yourself on your ability to go the extra mile for your colleagues

  • Flexibility - you're a reliable individual who is able to work flexibly across the week, including evenings, weekends and during peak holiday periods

  • True ambassador for our club - you have a willingness to develop expert knowledge about our club and history

You must be 18 years of age or older by Thursday 22nd October 2026 in order to apply for these positions.


Arsenal for Everyone

Arsenal for Everyone is our commitment to promoting and embracing equality, diversity and inclusion, so that everyone connected to the club feels like they belong to the same Arsenal family. We believe that diversity of background, skills and experience drives our success on and off the pitch. 


Disability Confident Leader

We are a Disability Confident Leader. We actively welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions. If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a ‘disabled person’ according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below. The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment decisions.

Application Closing Date - Friday 25th September 2026

Please note: we reserve the right to close the position early if application volumes are particularly high. We encourage you to get your application in sooner rather than later.

Updates on the status of your application will be sent via email, please routinely check your spam and junk folders, as occasionally emails sent via the Teamtailor platform will find themselves there.

Good luck!

job.title: Academy Nutritionist (Consultant Role)
job.html_description:
The Role

We are looking for an Academy Nutritionist to support our Academy Performance team on a part-time consulting basis and enhance and deliver a high-quality, age-appropriate nutrition service for U9-U14 Academy players based at Hale End.

You will play a key role in strengthening the existing nutrition framework to continue to support the health, development, and performance of our young players. This consultant role will contribute directly to our Academy’s overarching mission of creating the most challenging and caring football academy in the world.

Please note: this position is a consultant role on a part-time basis and is likely to be 2 days per week

Who we are

We are one of the most famous clubs in world football, with a rich heritage and history of success – read more about our history, here.

Beyond that, we are passionate about our local community and, behind the scenes, we have a wide variety of opportunities and career paths for all. We have a very defined purpose: to act for a winning team, culture and community. We achieve this by ensuring we are courageous in the pursuit of progress, we champion our community and each other, and that we do the right thing (even when no one is looking).

Our Commitment to Safeguarding

We are committed to ensuring that our environments for children, young people and adults at risk remain safe and inclusive. We therefore require successful candidates to complete a DBS check and other essential background checks prior to starting their employment. Depending on the responsibilities of the role, a DBS will be either a basic, standard, or enhanced check.

Your day-to-day

  • Deliver nutrition education sessions - you'll deliver theoretical and practical nutrition education sessions in line with the existing curriculum, enhancing nutrition education for players, parents & guardians, coaches and key stakeholders

  • Champion nutritional excellence - you will lead nutrition monitoring including food diary analysis and feedback, and you'll influence nutrition behaviours by being present at key meal and snack times

  • Lead nutrition clinics - you'll manage player and parent/guardian nutrition clinics for both injured and fit players

  • Oversee the Academy's food provision - you will contribute to menu planning and the improvement of food provision at Hale End

  • Collaborate with our restaurant staff - you'll liaise with Chefs and our Kitchen team to ensure appropriate nutrition timing and quality, and you will seek to contribute to the improvement of the Hale End restaurant environment

  • Liaise with external stakeholders - you will regularly communicate with schools to educate and improve nutrition provision

  • Provide support across matchdays - you'll assist in organising and arranging food provision for matchdays, tours and tournaments

  • Offer support across the wider department - you will attend and contribute to departmental meetings and will undertake any other activities as required by the Lead Academy Nutritionist and Head of Academy Performance

 

What we are looking for

  • Background in elite sport - you've previously applied your nutritional expertise within a professional sport setting

  • Credible expertise - you hold a MSc degree in Sport Nutrition and you're registered with The Sport and Exercise Nutrition Register (SENr) to a minimum of graduate level

  • Excellent communication skills - you're able to build impactful relationships and communicate your ideas clearly with both internal colleagues and external stakeholders

  • Organised and adaptable approach - you thrive when you're balancing competing priorities and are able to manage and organise your workload with ease

  • Professional mindset - you can act as an ambassador for our club and role model the Academy's values as well as the wider club values, and you're able to operate with discretion and confidentiality within your role

    Position of Trust - As someone in a position of trust role involving regular, direct contact with children or vulnerable adults you will be expected to uphold high standards of conduct to prevent abuse, including sexual, physical, or emotional harm. This role requires you to keep updated with both Club and FA Safeguarding training and education

Arsenal for Everyone

Arsenal for Everyone is our commitment to promoting and embracing equality, diversity and inclusion, so that everyone connected to the club feels like they belong to the same Arsenal family. We believe that diversity of background, skills and experience drives our success on and off the pitch. 


Disability Confident Leader

We are a Disability Confident Leader. We actively welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities and long-term health conditions. If you need disability-related adjustments to the recruitment process, please indicate this in your application.

If you are likely to meet the definition of being a ‘disabled person’ according to the Equality Act 2010, you may be eligible to apply for an interview via the Disability Confident Scheme - please indicate this in your application form below. The information you share with us about your health or disability will not be used in recruitment decisions.


Application Closing Date - Sunday 4th October 2026

Please note: we reserve the right to close the position early if application volumes are particularly high. We encourage you to get your application in sooner rather than later.

Updates on the status of your application will be sent via email, please routinely check your spam and junk folders, as occasionally emails sent via the Teamtailor platform will find themselves there.

Good luck!

job.title: Ticketing Manager
job.html_description:
The Ticketing Manager is responsible for the effective leadership and day-to-day management of AFC Bournemouth’s Ticket Office, ensuring a high standard of service, operational efficiency and an excellent supporter experience. The role will lead, develop and resource the team, ensuring the Ticket Office is well prepared to meet the demands of the club’s fixture and event programme. 
 
Working closely with the Chief Sales Officer and key stakeholders across the club, the Ticketing Manager will oversee ticketing activity across all competitions and events, balancing supporter needs with the club’s operational and commercial objectives while driving continuous improvement in ticketing processes and service delivery.

Working Requirements
  • Please note this role does require the incumbent to be available for contact outside of core working hours and be available to work weekends and all home fixtures throughout the season.
  • Availability during peak on-sale periods and high-demand fixtures. 
  • Lead and manage the AFC Bournemouth ticket office team, setting and maintaining high standards of customer service, professionalism and supporter experience. 
  • Act as the day-to-day line manager for the ticket office team, providing clear direction, regular feedback, coaching and performance management to ensure the team is engaged, knowledgeable and operating effectively. This includes casual members of ticket office staff. 
  • Recruit, onboard, train and develop ticket office colleagues, identifying individual strengths, development needs and skill sets to build a capable, resilient and high-performing team. 
  • Take overall responsibility for the effective organisation and resourcing of the ticket office, scheduling, ensuring appropriate staffing levels, skills and coverage to meet the demands of the football club and its varied fixture and event programme. 
  • Act as the primary point of contact for ticket office requirements across the club, working closely with departments including hospitality, operations, safety, commercial, marketing, media & communications, football operations, accounts and supporter services to understand requirements and deliver an effective, joined-up service. 
  • Coordinate interdepartmental ticketing requirements, ensuring key stakeholders are kept informed and that agreed processes, deadlines and priorities are clearly understood and delivered. 
  • Act as a senior point of escalation for supporter enquiries, complaints and concerns, taking ownership of complex or sensitive cases and ensuring they are resolved fairly, professionally and in line with club policies and values. 
  • Champion a supporter-first approach across the ticket office, using feedback, complaints and customer insight to identify opportunities to improve processes, communication and the overall supporter experience. 
  • Work closely with marketing and communications to ensure ticketing information, policies, deadlines and campaigns are communicated clearly, accurately and consistently across appropriate supporter channels. 
  • Work closely with the Chief Sales Officer to support the club’s wider ticketing objectives, contributing to strategies that maximise revenue and attendance while maintaining an excellent supporter experience. 
  • Support the planning and delivery of ticketing activity across Premier League fixtures, European competitions, cup competitions, hospitality requirements, commercial initiatives and other club events, ensuring the ticket office is appropriately prepared to meet operational demands. 
  • Maintain a strong understanding of Premier League, UEFA, FA, EFL and other relevant competition and regulatory requirements relating to ticketing and supporter management, ensuring the ticket office operates in accordance with applicable rules and club policies. 
  • Work closely with accounts to ensure appropriate financial controls and processes are followed within the ticket office, including reconciliation, refunds, invoicing, record keeping and reporting. 
  • Monitor ticket sales, supporter demand and operational performance, providing regular updates and insight to the Chief Sales Officer and relevant senior stakeholders. 
  • Identify opportunities to improve ticket office processes, team performance and supporter service, taking a proactive approach to resolving issues and implementing improvements. 
  • Ensure effective communication within the ticket office team, creating a positive, collaborative working environment where colleagues understand their responsibilities and feel supported to perform at their best. 
  • Develop and maintain effective working relationships with internal stakeholders and external partners, representing the ticket office professionally and ensuring the club's requirements are understood and delivered. 
  • Ensure the ticket office operates in accordance with the club’s policies and procedures, including health and safety, data protection, equality, diversity and inclusion requirements. 
  • Ensure in all matters you follow and actively promote the club’s equality policies and practices to ensure a welcoming, safe and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. 
  • To ensure the club’s mental health & wellbeing objectives are embedded in your department's actions, procedures and dealings and to have a good knowledge of the processes to support staff's mental health & wellbeing. 
  • To ensure commitment to the club’s safeguarding vision and to actively promote the policies within your department, embedding safeguarding into procedures.
  • Obligation to adhere to the club’s health and safety policy and procedures. 
  • Responsibility to comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, and all related Company policies, taking reasonable care for their own safety and that of others, reporting hazards or incidents, following safe systems of work, and co-operating with all training and emergency procedures.
  • To ensure the club’s equality aims, action plan and policies are in evidence in all departmental actions, procedures and dealings. 
The duties and responsibilities described are not a comprehensive list and additional tasks may be assigned to the employee from time to time; or the scope of the job may change as necessitated by business demands.
Essential: 
  • Proven experience of leading, managing and developing a team, including the ability to motivate colleagues and maintain high standards of performance and customer service. 
  • Experience of managing dynamic, high-volume sales environments, with the ability to adapt to changing priorities, demands and supporter requirements. 
  • Excellent customer service and communication skills, with the ability to remain calm, professional and solutions-focused when dealing with pressure, challenging situations and complex supporter enquiries. 
  • Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines and complex ticketing requirements accurately and effectively. 
  • Proactive approach with strong problem-solving skills, demonstrating initiative, sound judgement and the ability to identify and implement improvements to processes and ways of working. 
  • Excellent relationship-building and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to develop effective working relationships across multiple internal departments and with external partners. 
  • Experience supporting live sales and event environments, with the ability to identify issues, make sound decisions and resolve problems effectively in real time.
Desirable:
  • Strong knowledge and practical experience of working in a football or sports ticketing environment, ideally gained in a supervisory or management capacity. 
  • Advanced knowledge of ticketing systems and processes, including seat mapping, pricing structures, allocations, fulfilment methods and digital ticketing. 
  • Experience working within professional football, particularly the Premier League or other elite competition environments. 
  • Experience using SeatGeek as a primary ticketing platform and TEAMcard for access control. 
  • Knowledge and understanding of domestic and European football ticketing regulations and competition requirements. 
  • Free onsite parking.

job.plain_text_description:
The Ticketing Manager is responsible for the effective leadership and day-to-day management of AFC Bournemouth’s Ticket Office, ensuring a high standard of service, operational efficiency and an excellent supporter experience. The role will lead, develop and resource the team, ensuring the Ticket Office is well prepared to meet the demands of the club’s fixture and event programme.
Working closely with the Chief Sales Officer and key stakeholders across the club, the Ticketing Manager will oversee ticketing activity across all competitions and events, balancing supporter needs with the club’s operational and commercial objectives while driving continuous improvement in ticketing processes and service delivery.
Working Requirements
- Please note this role does require the incumbent to be available for contact outside of core working hours and be available to work weekends and all home fixtures throughout the season. - Availability during peak on-sale periods and high-demand fixtures.
- Lead and manage the AFC Bournemouth ticket office team, setting and maintaining high standards of customer service, professionalism and supporter experience. - Act as the day-to-day line manager for the ticket office team, providing clear direction, regular feedback, coaching and performance management to ensure the team is engaged, knowledgeable and operating effectively. This includes casual members of ticket office staff. - Recruit, onboard, train and develop ticket office colleagues, identifying individual strengths, development needs and skill sets to build a capable, resilient and high-performing team. - Take overall responsibility for the effective organisation and resourcing of the ticket office, scheduling, ensuring appropriate staffing levels, skills and coverage to meet the demands of the football club and its varied fixture and event programme. - Act as the primary point of contact for ticket office requirements across the club, working closely with departments including hospitality, operations, safety, commercial, marketing, media & communications, football operations, accounts and supporter services to understand requirements and deliver an effective, joined-up service. - Coordinate interdepartmental ticketing requirements, ensuring key stakeholders are kept informed and that agreed processes, deadlines and priorities are clearly understood and delivered. - Act as a senior point of escalation for supporter enquiries, complaints and concerns, taking ownership of complex or sensitive cases and ensuring they are resolved fairly, professionally and in line with club policies and values. - Champion a supporter-first approach across the ticket office, using feedback, complaints and customer insight to identify opportunities to improve processes, communication and the overall supporter experience. - Work closely with marketing and communications to ensure ticketing information, policies, deadlines and campaigns are communicated clearly, accurately and consistently across appropriate supporter channels. - Work closely with the Chief Sales Officer to support the club’s wider ticketing objectives, contributing to strategies that maximise revenue and attendance while maintaining an excellent supporter experience. - Support the planning and delivery of ticketing activity across Premier League fixtures, European competitions, cup competitions, hospitality requirements, commercial initiatives and other club events, ensuring the ticket office is appropriately prepared to meet operational demands. - Maintain a strong understanding of Premier League, UEFA, FA, EFL and other relevant competition and regulatory requirements relating to ticketing and supporter management, ensuring the ticket office operates in accordance with applicable rules and club policies. - Work closely with accounts to ensure appropriate financial controls and processes are followed within the ticket office, including reconciliation, refunds, invoicing, record keeping and reporting. - Monitor ticket sales, supporter demand and operational performance, providing regular updates and insight to the Chief Sales Officer and relevant senior stakeholders. - Identify opportunities to improve ticket office processes, team performance and supporter service, taking a proactive approach to resolving issues and implementing improvements. - Ensure effective communication within the ticket office team, creating a positive, collaborative working environment where colleagues understand their responsibilities and feel supported to perform at their best. - Develop and maintain effective working relationships with internal stakeholders and external partners, representing the ticket office professionally and ensuring the club's requirements are understood and delivered. - Ensure the ticket office operates in accordance with the club’s policies and procedures, including health and safety, data protection, equality, diversity and inclusion requirements. - Ensure in all matters you follow and actively promote the club’s equality policies and practices to ensure a welcoming, safe and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. - To ensure the club’s mental health & wellbeing objectives are embedded in your department's actions, procedures and dealings and to have a good knowledge of the processes to support staff's mental health & wellbeing. - To ensure commitment to the club’s safeguarding vision and to actively promote the policies within your department, embedding safeguarding into procedures. - Obligation to adhere to the club’s health and safety policy and procedures. - Responsibility to comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, and all related Company policies, taking reasonable care for their own safety and that of others, reporting hazards or incidents, following safe systems of work, and co-operating with all training and emergency procedures. - To ensure the club’s equality aims, action plan and policies are in evidence in all departmental actions, procedures and dealings.

job.title: Women's Team Medical and Performance Manager
job.location: AFC Bournemouth Performance Centre, Wimborne, Wimborne, Dorset
job.html_description:
AFC Bournemouth Women are looking to recruit a Medical and Performance Manager to coordinate the effective delivery of Medical & Performance services across the First Team and Development Squad. Reporting to both the Director of Medical and Performance and Head of Women’s Football, this role acts as a central point of co-ordination between medical, rehabilitation, physical performance and wider player-support practitioners, helping ensure clear communication, effective processes and consistent standards across the programme. The role supports an integrated multidisciplinary approach that promotes player health, availability, development and performance, while enabling individual practitioners to focus on delivering high quality support within their respective areas of expertise.

 WOMEN’S TEAM VALUES 
  • Professionalism: Always acting with integrity and respect for the badge in a competent and reliable manner.
  • Togetherness: Working collaboratively through high levels of communication in a manner that supports an environment where everyone feels included, respected and valued. 
  • Opportunity: Providing fair and equitable chances to all individuals by encouraging a growth mindset through empowering the natural abilities of others in service of the overall mission. 
  • Team First: Prioritising the team beyond personal or individual interests. 
  • Co-ordinate the day-to-day Medical & Performance provision across the Women's First Team and Development Squad. 
  • Act as the central communication point between Medical & Performance practitioners, football staff and the wider Club. 
  • Co-ordinate regular multidisciplinary meetings, ensuring clear information sharing, agreed actions and appropriate follow-up. 
  • Support effective planning and integration of medical, rehabilitation, physical performance and player-support services. 
  • Ensure appropriate processes are in place for player availability, screening, rehabilitation, referrals, appointments and return-to-play coordination. 
  • Support consistent documentation, professional standards and governance across the programme, escalating matters where appropriate. 
  • Co-ordinate player medical and performance processes associated with recruitment and signing, in collaboration with relevant practitioners and Club leadership. 
  • Work with the Director of Medical & Performance and wider AFCB Medical & Performance department to align appropriate systems, standards and best practice. 
  • Support the organisation of equipment, facilities, technology and external services required for effective delivery. 
  • Foster an integrated and collaborative environment in which practitioners are enabled to focus on their professional responsibilities and players receive coordinated support.
  • Depending on experience and organisational requirements, provide appropriate coordination, supervision and/or line-management support to members of the Women's Medical & Performance team 
  • As a member of staff to ensure in all matters, you follow and actively promote the club’s mental health policies and practices to ensure an open, non-judgmental and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. 
  • As a member of staff to ensure that you adhere to the club’s safeguarding policies and procedures and are committed to our safeguarding values, creating a safe and positive environment for all those who interact with the club.
  • Obligation to adhere to the club’s health and safety policy and procedures. 
  • Responsibility to comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, and all related Company policies, taking reasonable care for their own safety and that of others, reporting hazards or incidents, following safe systems of work, and co-operating with all training and emergency procedures.
  • As a member of staff to ensure in all matters you follow and actively promote the club’s equality policies and practices to ensure a welcoming, safe and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. 
The duties and responsibilities described are not a comprehensive list and additional tasks may be assigned to the employee from time to time; or the scope of the job may change as necessitated by business demands.
 Essential 
  • Degree in at least one relevant medical or performance discipline, which may include medicine, physiotherapy, sports therapy, rehabilitation, sport science, strength and conditioning, psychology, wellbeing or a related field. 
  • Relevant professional registration, accreditation or membership appropriate to the candidate’s primary discipline. 
  • Experience working within elite football or a comparable high-performance sporting environment. 
  • Safeguarding and appropriate DBS clearance. 
  • Strong understanding of professional boundaries, clinical governance, confidentiality, safeguarding and duty of care. 
Desirable 
  • Postgraduate qualification in a relevant medical, performance, psychology, wellbeing, leadership or management discipline. 
  • Knowledge of relevant FA, WNL and WSL medical and performance support requirements. 
  • Experience working within Women’s National or Super Leagues. 
  • Experience leading, managing or coordinating a multidisciplinary medical and performance team. 
  • UK Anti-Doping Introduction to Clean Sport certificate, or willingness to complete.
Key Competencies
  • Ability to coordinate people and processes effectively within a multidisciplinary environment. 
  • Strong organisational, communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to prioritise effectively in a dynamic environment. 
  • High level of written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to foster strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders. 
  • Previous experience of line management or multidisciplinary team leadership. 
  • Free onsite parking.
  • Season ticket and allocation of complimentary/purchased tickets (subject to availability).
  • Subsidised lunches and complimentary healthy snacks throughout the day.
  • Discounts at the club Superstore.
  • Access to Health Cash Plan with Simplyhealth.
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Contribution towards eye tests and glasses.
  • Discounts and benefits from partners and local businesses.
  • Club pension & Life Assurance Scheme.
  • Paid parental leave (bank of five days per year).
  • Club events or other social events throughout the year run by our club social team.
  • Paid volunteer opportunities (2 days per year).
  • Paid day’s leave on your birthday.

job.title: Academy Driver (Casual)
job.location: AFC Bournemouth Performance Centre, Wimborne, Wimborne, Dorset
job.html_description:
To transport Academy players to and from all Academy activity, around Bournemouth and nationally.

Academy Values: 
  • Players First: every player valued. Every decision made with care. 
  • Togetherness: working in a prosocial manner as part of a wider team – willing to contribute beyond own interests. 
  • Integrity: carrying out academy and club values in an open and honest manner. 
  • Accountability: willing to take responsibility for actions in a manner which allows learning, growth and reflection. 

  • Transport Academy Players from various pick-up points in the Bournemouth area to and from AFC Bournemouth Performance Centre. Pick up points include but are not limited to: Vitality Stadium, Bournemouth Train Station, Player Accommodation.  
  • Be available to transport Academy players to venues around the country for away fixtures at weekends. 
  • To be available to transport Academy players to other venues as and when needed. 
  • Liaise with the Academy Operations & Player Care teams around weekly schedules and bus registers.  
  • Daily & weekly vehicle checks to be undertaken prior to any journey. Any faults are to be reported in the first instance to the Academy, and maintain the cleanliness of the vehicles. 
  • Provide transport for Academy Players in a safe and lawful manner, fully compliant with the Highway Code and other regulations applying to passenger and minibus transport.  
  • As a casual member of staff to ensure in all matters, you follow and actively promote the club’s mental health policies and practices to ensure an open, non-judgmental and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. 
  • As a casual member of staff to ensure that you to adhere to the club’s safeguarding policies and procedures and are committed to our safeguarding values, creating a safe and positive environment for all those who interact with the club. 
  • Obligation to adhere to the club’s health and safety policy and procedures. 
  • Responsibility to comply with the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, the Regulatory Reform (Fire Safety) Order 2005, and all related Company policies, taking reasonable care for their own safety and that of others, reporting hazards or incidents, following safe systems of work, and co-operating with all training and emergency procedures.
  • As a casual member of staff to ensure in all matters you follow and actively promote the club’s equality policies and practices to ensure a welcoming, safe and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club. 
The duties and responsibilities described are not a comprehensive list and additional tasks may be assigned to the employee from time to time; or the scope of the job may change as necessitated by business demands.
  • Valid UK Driving Licence, including D1 
  • Experience in driving 17-seater minibuses 
  • Experience in driving sports teams or young people (desirable)

job.title: Concourse Bar Staff (Casual)
job.html_description:
We are recruiting staff to serve food, confectionery, hot /cold drinks, etc.
 The shifts are approx. 4 - 6 hours home match day only (usually Saturday ko. 3.00pm.).
Staff will be expected to work at a fast pace as we only have a smalltime frame to serve the supporters.

The stadium is very busy on a match day but there is a good atmosphere within the team and you get to know the supporters.

Experience is a bonus, but not essential as full training given onsite.
  • Duties include using tills, recording information, replenishing stock, ensuring your work area is clean and tidy.
  •  You will also be expected to handle food this can include an element of cooking.
  •  You will be expected to work as part of a team as there are 22 concourse bars and kiosk around the stadium.
  • Customer care is very important to us, so you will be expected to be polite and helpful to all individual customers..
  • As a casual worker you must adhere to the club’s safeguarding policies and procedures and are committed to our safeguarding values, creating a safe and positive environment for all those who interact with the club. 
  • Obligation to adhere to the club’s health and safety policy and procedures. 
  • Actively promote the club’s equality policies and practices to ensure a welcoming, safe and inclusive environment for everyone engaged with the club.

job.title: Casual Football Coach - Perth, MCFC Football Education Australia
job.html_description:
Based in Perth, Australia, this casual role gives you the chance to deliver engaging football education sessions for children across the Manchester City Perth Football Education Program. You will help create a positive, inclusive and development-focused environment where young players can enjoy the game, build confidence and learn through high-quality coaching.

 

Who We Are

 

Manchester City is a football club rooted in East Manchester, with a story that began in 1880 and continues to grow today. Built on resilience, belief and togetherness, success on the pitch is driven by the moments and memories shared with millions of Fans around the world. City is known for its bravery, its determination to the very end and its strong connection to where we come from. With Mancunian roots and a global outlook, we are shaped by our Fans and driven by a long-term vision, from developing future talent to supporting the communities we call home. Together, we are creating the next chapter, the City way.

 

Within the Manchester City Perth Football Education Program, we deliver football experiences that are welcoming, well-structured and enjoyable for children and families across Western Australia. Our coaches play an important part in bringing the Club's philosophy to life through sessions that support confidence, learning and a love of the game.

 

The Role

 

This role sits at the heart of the Perth program and is focused on delivering high-quality football education sessions for children in a way that feels inclusive, fun and purposeful. You will help young players develop their skills, enjoy their football and feel supported in an environment that reflects Manchester City's coaching values.

 

You will plan and deliver age-appropriate sessions aligned to the Manchester City coaching philosophy and curriculum, working across multiple venues in Perth as required. Day to day, you will keep sessions organised, safe and engaging, while also supporting player progress through simple reporting, reflection and feedback.

 

You will work closely with the Head Coach and wider programme team to maintain consistent standards and a positive experience for children, parents and carers. This role also involves communicating clearly with families, contributing to programme improvement and taking part in ongoing learning and development as the programme grows.

 

What You’ll Bring

 

⚽ A recognised coaching qualification, with a minimum UEFA C or AFC C Licence.

⚽ Experience coaching children or young players in a grassroots, community or football education setting.

⚽ Ability to plan and deliver inclusive, engaging sessions that support enjoyment, learning and confidence.

⚽ Clear and effective communication skills when working with children, parents, carers and colleagues.

⚽ Ability to work flexibly across afternoons, evenings and weekends, and to travel between Perth venues as required.

⚽ A valid Western Australian Working With Children Check, or willingness to obtain one, together with the ability to work exclusively for Manchester City in Western Australia and not with other football or coaching organisations while in this role.

 

Why Choose Us

 

Working at Manchester City means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

 

As part of our Perth Football Education Program, you will have the opportunity to coach within a global football environment that values player development, inclusion and quality delivery. You will be supported to bring the Manchester City coaching philosophy to life for children and families across Western Australia.

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 30 September. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

 

Please note that successful applicants will be expected to work exclusively for Manchester City in Western Australia and not provide coaching services for other football or coaching organisations while engaged in this role.

 

Equal Opportunities

 

City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.

All CFG recruitment communications originate from @cityfootball.com email addresses. If you receive communications from Gmail, Outlook.com or other personal email services claiming to represent CFG, please verify with the hiring team. Employment is subject to the provision of proof of eligibility to work in Australia.

Due to our safeguarding promise, all Perth-based CFG roles will be subject to any relevant safeguarding or working-with-children checks required for the job role and responsibilities.

job.title: Casual Applied Data Analyst
job.html_description:
Based in Manchester, this part-time, casual role is a great opportunity for a current Master’s or PhD student to gain hands-on experience in applied data analysis within an elite sporting environment. You will support Manchester City Women’s Performance Services team by helping to collect, clean, analyse and report on health and performance data that informs day-to-day decision-making and supports player availability and on-pitch performance.

 

Who We Are

 

Manchester City Women is a team driven by ambition, belief and a desire to keep pushing the game forward. Founded in 1988 and relaunched in 2014, we have grown into a consistent force in the women’s game, competing at the highest level in the UK and Europe. Progress, performance and pride sit at the heart of everything we do. With Mancunian roots and a global outlook, we are shaped by our Fans and driven by a long-term vision, from developing future talent to supporting the communities we call home. Together, we are building what comes next, the City way.

Within our Performance Services team, we work closely with practitioners and CFG Football Intelligence colleagues to support player health, physical performance and decision-making through reliable data and meaningful insight. We are focused on building clear, well-governed reporting that helps the team make informed decisions every day.

 

The Role

 

This role plays an important part in helping our Performance Services team capture, manage and interpret the data that supports player health and physical performance. You will work with practitioners to make sure information is accurate, timely and well organised, giving the team confidence in the data they use to inform decisions.

Day to day, you will support the collection, cleaning, validation and analysis of performance data from core systems, tests and outputs. You will help maintain athlete management systems, produce clear reports and summaries, and contribute to the development of frameworks and methods that make our analysis more useful in practice.

You will also work closely with Manchester City Women’s Performance Services team and CFG Football Intelligence colleagues to turn data into practical insight, with a particular focus on female athlete health and performance. Careful handling of sensitive information, clear communication and a thoughtful approach to context will all be central to how you support the wider team.

 

What You’ll Bring

 

⚽You will be a careful, collaborative and curious analyst who enjoys working with data in a performance environment. You will be comfortable balancing detail with pace, communicating clearly and turning information into practical insight for practitioners.

⚽Currently studying towards a relevant Master’s degree or PhD in a quantitative discipline such as data science, sports science, statistics, mathematics, computer science, epidemiology or a related area.

⚽An understanding of core data-analysis and statistical concepts.

⚽ Experience using at least one analytical tool or programming language, such as Python, R, SQL, MATLAB or a similar platform.

⚽ Competence using Microsoft Excel or similar spreadsheet software for data cleaning, organisation and analysis.

⚽ Ability to communicate analytical findings clearly to a non-technical audience and work collaboratively with a range of practitioners.

⚽A careful, methodical approach to data entry, validation and quality assurance, with the ability to organise work effectively and manage recurring tasks alongside academic commitments.

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by Wednesday 23rd September. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

 

Equal Opportunities

 

City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.

All CFG recruitment communications originate from @cityfootball.com email addresses. If you receive communications from Gmail, Outlook.com or other personal email services claiming to represent CFG, please verify with the hiring team. Employment is subject to the provision of proof of eligibility to work in the UK.

Due to our safeguarding promise, all UK-based CFG roles will be subject to a DBS check upon commencing employment with us. This will be either a basic, standard or enhanced check depending on the job role and responsibilities.

job.title: Commercial Finance Manager
job.html_description:
Based in Manchester, this full time,18-month maternity cover role will help shape the financial performance of Manchester City’s matchday and non-matchday commercial operations. You will turn financial data into clear insight that supports decisions across ticketing, hospitality, catering and major stadium events, while helping the Commercial Finance team deliver sustainable revenue and EBITDA performance in a collaborative hybrid environment with a minimum of three days per week in the office.

 

 

Who We Are

 

 

Manchester City is a football club rooted in East Manchester, with a story that began in 1880 and continues to grow today. Built on resilience, belief and togetherness, success on the pitch is driven by the moments and memories shared with millions of Fans around the world. City is known for its bravery, its determination to the very end and its strong connection to where we come from. With Mancunian roots and a global outlook, we are shaped by our Fans and driven by a long-term vision, from developing future talent to supporting the communities we call home. Together, we are creating the next chapter, the City way.

Our Commercial Finance team supports the financial management of matchday and non-matchday revenue across the stadium. Working closely with colleagues in ticketing, hospitality, catering and events, the team provides the insight, challenge and planning needed to help Manchester City make informed commercial decisions and deliver memorable experiences for our Fans and visitors.

 

 

The Role

 

 

As Commercial Finance Manager, you will provide strategic financial support across Manchester City’s stadium revenue generation. Your analysis will help colleagues understand performance, identify opportunities and make timely decisions across ticketing, hospitality, catering and non-matchday events, including concerts and future major events such as Euro 2028 activity.

You will lead the co-ordination of budgets and forecasts across matchday areas, oversee P&L management and monitor product performance and margins. You will translate complex financial information into clear, accessible reporting, support corrective action where needed and contribute to the team’s ongoing process improvements.

The role is also responsible for managing and developing a Finance Analyst. You will build trusted relationships with a broad range of stakeholders, communicate financial findings with confidence and work closely with the Finance Business Partner – Stadium Finance to support the department’s objectives and long-term plans.

 

 

What You’ll Bring

 

 

⚽ Relevant finance capability gained through an accounting qualification, relevant degree or equivalent practical experience.

⚽ Experience applying commercial finance expertise to budgeting, forecasting and P&L management.

⚽ Data analysis capability, with the ability to turn financial information into useful insight and recommendations.

⚽ Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, with confidence presenting information clearly.

⚽ Clear and effective communication skills, with the ability to build productive relationships and influence a range of stakeholders.

⚽ A proactive and solutions-focused approach, with the ability to organise work and deliver accurate, high-quality outputs to agreed deadlines.

 

 

 

Why Choose Us

 

 

Working at Manchester City means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.

Manchester-based employees also benefit from free on-site parking, complimentary breakfast and lunch, and access to a range of sports and leisure clubs.

You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.

 

 

How to Apply

 

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 28 September. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

The recruitment process will begin with a Talent Acquisition sift and hiring manager review. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a 30-minute Teams interview and asked to complete a task provided in advance. Finalists will then attend a 45–60 minute interview on site in Manchester.

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

 

 

Equal Opportunities

 

 

City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.

All CFG recruitment communications originate from @cityfootball.com email addresses. If you receive communications from Gmail, Outlook.com or other personal email services claiming to represent CFG, please verify with the hiring team. Employment is subject to the provision of proof of eligibility to work in the UK.

Due to our safeguarding promise, all UK-based CFG roles will be subject to a DBS check upon commencing employment with us. This will be either a basic, standard or enhanced check depending on the job role and responsibilities.

Based in Manchester, this full time,18-month maternity cover role will help shape the financial performance of Manchester City’s matchday and non-matchday commercial operations. You will turn financial data into clear insight that supports decisions across ticketing, hospitality, catering and major stadium events, while helping the Commercial Finance team deliver sustainable revenue and EBITDA performance in a collaborative hybrid environment with a minimum of three days per week in the office.

Manchester City is a football club rooted in East Manchester, with a story that began in 1880 and continues to grow today. Together, we are creating the next chapter, the City way.
Our Commercial Finance team supports the financial management of matchday and non-matchday revenue across the stadium. Working closely with colleagues in ticketing, hospitality, catering and events, the team provides the insight, challenge and planning needed to help Manchester City make informed commercial decisions and deliver memorable experiences for our Fans and visitors.
The Role
As Commercial Finance Manager, you will provide strategic financial support across Manchester City’s stadium revenue generation. Your analysis will help colleagues understand performance, identify opportunities and make timely decisions across ticketing, hospitality, catering and non-matchday events, including concerts and future major events such as Euro 2028 activity.
You will lead the co-ordination of budgets and forecasts across matchday areas, oversee P&L management and monitor product performance and margins. You will translate complex financial information into clear, accessible reporting, support corrective action where needed and contribute to the team’s ongoing process improvements.

You will build trusted relationships with a broad range of stakeholders, communicate financial findings with confidence and work closely with the Finance Business Partner – Stadium Finance to support the department’s objectives and long-term plans.

job.title: Academy Driver and Logistics Assistant
job.html_description:
Based at the City Football Academy in Manchester, this permanent full-time role supports the safe and reliable delivery of transport for Academy players, staff, trialists and families. You will combine professional driving with thoughtful administration, helping every journey run smoothly while contributing to a welcoming, well-organised environment for everyone connected to the Academy.

 

Who We Are

 

Manchester City is a football club rooted in East Manchester, with a story that began in 1880 and continues to grow today. Built on resilience, belief and togetherness, success on the pitch is driven by the moments and memories shared with millions of Fans around the world. City is known for its bravery, its determination to the very end and its strong connection to where we come from. With Mancunian roots and a global outlook, we are shaped by our Fans and driven by a long-term vision, from developing future talent to supporting the communities we call home. Together, we are creating the next chapter, the City way.

 

Within our Academy, the Transport and Administration team helps create the conditions for young players and staff to focus on development and performance. Through safe transport, accurate coordination and a professional approach to every interaction, the team plays an important part in the daily experience of players, families and Academy colleagues.

 

The Role

 

As Academy Driver and Logistics Assistant, you will help coordinate the Academy's day-to-day transport service, ensuring players, staff, guests and families can travel safely, comfortably and on time. Your work will support scholar and Day Release runs, staff transport and the wider logistics of an Academy operating at a high standard.

 

Alongside driving, you will maintain schedules, records, reports and documentation, keeping information accurate and processes easy to follow. You will also help monitor departmental vehicles, report faults, coordinate maintenance and ensure vehicle records remain current. There will be opportunities to improve transport processes and administrative systems as the needs of the Academy evolve.

 

You will build positive working relationships with players, families, staff, agents and representatives, sharing relevant information appropriately where player behaviour, welfare or development is concerned. You will also support tours, tournaments and Academy events, including meeting and greeting trialists and prospective signings and helping provide a professional first impression. The role involves safeguarding responsibilities and flexibility to work variable and unsociable hours when operationally required.

 

What You’ll Bring

 

  • A clean UK driving licence, with the confidence and experience to provide safe, professional transport for a range of passengers.
  • Experience working in an administrative environment, with the ability to manage schedules, records, reports and documentation accurately.
  • Competence with Microsoft Office and everyday computer-based administrative systems.
  • Clear and effective communication skills, including a professional approach to meeting and greeting players, families, guests and colleagues.
  • A flexible and confidential approach, with the ability to respond calmly to changing operational needs and work variable or unsociable hours frequently when required.

 

Why Choose Us

 

Working at Manchester City means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

 

As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.

 

Manchester-based employees also benefit from free on-site parking, complimentary breakfast and lunch, and access to a range of sports and leisure clubs.

 

You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 29 September. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

 

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

 

Equal Opportunities

 

City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.

job.title: Head of Premium Hospitality Sales
job.html_description:
Based in Manchester, this permanent full-time role leads new premium sales growth across football matchdays, concerts and major stadium events at the Etihad Stadium. You will shape the acquisition strategy for premium hospitality, build relationships and lead a sales team that turns demand into meaningful commercial growth.

 

Who We Are

 

Founded in 2013, City Football Group is the world’s leading private owner and operator of football clubs, with teams across the globe connected by a shared belief in doing things differently. Alongside our clubs, we invest in football-related businesses and build partnerships that help the game, and the communities around it, thrive. Everything we do is guided by our purpose: empowering better lives through football. Rooted in more than a century of “City” football, we are proud of the role our clubs play locally and globally, creating positive impact on and off the pitch.

 

Within our Matchday and Major Stadium Events department, we create premium experiences across football, concerts and major events at the Etihad Stadium. Our commercial teams work together to connect clients with memorable experiences while delivering sustainable growth for the Group.

 

The Role

 

As Head of Premium Hospitality Sales, you will own the new business strategy and sales performance for our premium hospitality portfolio. You will be responsible for growing revenue from premium inventory across matchdays and major events, using a clear view of pipeline, conversion and demand to maximise opportunity and support the commercial goals of the stadium.

 

You will translate the wider growth strategy into a practical 12-month sales plan, balancing inbound and outbound activity and adapting priorities as inventory, customer demand and performance trends evolve. You will lead senior sales conversations, pitches and negotiations, developing tailored propositions for high-value and bespoke opportunities across boxes, lounges, VIP and experiential hospitality.

 

Alongside your own commercial contribution, you will lead, coach and develop a high-performing premium new-business sales team. You will embed clear targets, consistent sales processes, effective CRM and pipeline management, accurate forecasting and a disciplined approach to prospecting and conversion. Working closely with Marketing, Partnerships, Operations and the wider hospitality team, you will help ensure a seamless journey from initial engagement through to delivery and long-term client growth.

 

An exciting opportunity to join City and lead the growth of premium hospitality sales across football matchdays, concerts and major stadium events, helping create exceptional experiences for our Fans and clients.

 

 

What You’ll Bring

 

  • Experience in premium hospitality business-to-business or business-to-consumer sales.
  • Experience leading, supporting and developing a sales team through clear goals and consistent ways of working.
  • A disciplined sales operating rhythm, including weekly pipeline reviews, deal coaching, prospecting sessions and individual performance conversations.
  • Proven ability for balancing new-business acquisition with renewal, retention, upgrades and account growth.
  • Excellent negotiation, influencing and closing skills, with confidence in senior-level sales conversations.
  • Commercial judgement and the ability to manage targets, forecasting and reporting, supported by consistent CRM usage and clearly defined sales stages.
  • A passion for innovation with the ability to collaborate across commercial, marketing and event teams.

 

Why Choose Us

 

Working at City Football Group means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

 

As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.

 

Manchester-based employees also benefit from free on-site parking, complimentary breakfast and lunch, and access to a range of sports and leisure clubs.

 

You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 2 October 2026. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.

 

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

 

Equal Opportunities

 

City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.

All CFG recruitment communications originate from @cityfootball.com email addresses. If you receive communications from Gmail, Outlook.com or other personal email services claiming to represent CFG, please verify with the hiring team. Employment is subject to the provision of proof of eligibility to work in the UK.

Due to our safeguarding promise, all UK-based CFG roles will be subject to a DBS check upon commencing employment with us. This will be either a basic, standard or enhanced check depending on the job role and responsibilities.

job.title: Kit Assistant
job.html_description:
Help keep Manchester City Academy football moving by making sure players and staff have the right kit, in the right place, at the right time. Based at Manchester City Football Academy in Manchester, this full-time permanent role offers the chance to support a busy, varied operation across training, matchdays and team travel.

 

Who We Are

 

Manchester City is a football club rooted in East Manchester, with a story that began in 1880 and continues to grow today. Built on resilience, belief and togetherness, success on the pitch is driven by the moments and memories shared with millions of Fans around the world.

 

City is known for its bravery, its determination to the very end and its strong connection to where we come from. With Mancunian roots and a global outlook, we are shaped by our Fans and driven by a long-term vision, from developing future talent to supporting the communities we call home. Together, we are creating the next chapter, the City way.

 

The Academy Kit team plays an important part in creating the conditions for young players and staff to prepare, train and compete. Supporting kit requirements across 26 age groups, the team combines careful organisation with practical, hands-on service to help each programme run smoothly.

 

The Role

 

As Kit Assistant, you will support the Academy Kit Manager with the supply and preparation of training and matchday kit. Your work will have a direct impact on players and staff, helping them prepare for training, fixtures and travel with the right kit available at the right time.

 

You will organize match and training kit, arrange kit printing, manage daily training kit requirements and maintain high housekeeping standards at the Academy. You will also deliver used kit to the laundry throughout the day, follow kit-supplier requirements for different training uses and travel when and where the role requires.

 

Working as part of a supportive team, you will build effective relationships with colleagues across the Academy and provide a professional, service-focused response to changing needs. The role operates on a rota, with flexible hours to meet business requirements, including early and late starts, weekend work and matchdays; there may also be opportunities for international travel with Academy teams.

 

What You’ll Bring

 

⚽IT proficiency and the ability to use computerised stock-taking or record-keeping systems accurately.

⚽A clean driving licence and confidence driving as part of the role, including supporting kit deliveries and other team requirements.

⚽Ability to organise kit and equipment carefully so Players and Staff have what they need in a timely way.

⚽Careful attention to detail, with a practical approach to maintaining high housekeeping and kit-management standards.

⚽A flexible approach to working hours, including early starts, late finishes, weekends and matchdays when required.

⚽Self-management and a professional, service-focused approach when supporting colleagues, Players and Staff.

 

 

Why Choose Us

 

Working at Manchester City means being supported to do your best, with the flexibility and encouragement to look after your wellbeing. We are committed to helping our people learn, grow and thrive in a culture built on collaboration, openness and hard work.

 

As part of our team, you will receive 26 days’ annual leave plus a day off for your birthday, private healthcare and dental cover, and an annual discretionary bonus. You will also have access to a Health Cash Plan, Employee Assistance Programme with 24/7 GP support, and a company pension and life assurance.

 

Manchester-based employees also benefit from free on-site parking, complimentary breakfast and lunch, and access to a range of sports and leisure clubs.You can enjoy a range of additional benefits, including cycle to work, Give As You Earn, discounted match tickets, savings in the City Store, a free City+ subscription, stadium tour discounts, and wider retail and lifestyle offers.

 

How to Apply

 

If this role sounds like it is for you, we would love to hear from you. To apply, please submit your application via our careers site by 25th September 2026. We encourage you to apply as soon as you can.The recruitment process will include an initial application screening followed by first-stage interviews for shortlisted candidates.

 

We work with a select group of agency partners and do not accept unsolicited applications. Any CVs submitted without prior agreement will be treated as a direct application.

 

Equal Opportunities

 

City Football Group promotes equal opportunities in employment and we positively welcome applications from all candidates regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation.

 

We will screen all applicants and select candidates whose skills and experience seem to meet our needs. We will carefully consider your application during the initial screening and will contact you only if you are selected for an interview. If you require reasonable adjustments or any support throughout the process, please contact hiring@cityfootball.com and we will be happy to help.
