job.title: Academy Goalkeeping Coach (Part Time)
job.html_description:
We are seeking an enthusiastic and dedicated Foundation Phase Goalkeeping Coach to join our Academy coaching team for the 2026/27 season. The successful candidate will play a key role in delivering the Academy Goalkeeping Coaching Programme, supporting the development of young goalkeepers within the Foundation Phase and ensuring a smooth transition between the Pre-Academy, Foundation Phase, and Youth Development Phase.

Working within a player-centred environment, you will be responsible for planning, delivering, and reviewing high-quality coaching sessions that support the technical, tactical, physical, and psychological development of our goalkeepers. You will work closely with Academy staff to create a positive learning environment that maximises each player's potential.

This is a fixed-term contract for the 2026/27 season, based on 18 hours per week, with the potential for the role to be extended into the 2027/28 season. This is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious coach looking to contribute to a progressive Academy programme and support the development of the next generation of goalkeepers.

Responsibilities

The Academy Goalkeeping Coach must:
  • Be player/person centred & individualised in their approach 
  • Have a strong understanding of goalkeeper coaching & player development principles 
  • Have strong communication skills with young players, their parents and colleagues 
  • Have excellent Technical/Tactical Goalkeeping detail 
  • Be pro-active & hard working 
  • Be open and honest with feedback
  • Be highly motivated & passionate about supporting young goalkeepers 
  • Be willing to share work and learning with others 
  • Have a desire to engage in reflective practice 
  • Hold a UEFA B Goalkeeper Coaching Licence 
  • Hold a UEFA B Coaching Licence 
  • Hold an up-to-date Emergency First Aid in Football (EFAiF) Certificate through The FA 
  • Hold an up-to-date FA Safeguarding Children Certificate

Ideally, the Academy Goalkeeping Coach will:
  • Hold a UEFA A Goalkeeper Coaching Licence 
  • Hold the FA Youth Award 
  • Hold the FA Advanced Youth Award

Requirements

The Academy Goalkeeping Coach (‘AGC’) is employed to prepare, deliver and review Goalkeeper coaching activities in line with the Academy’s Performance Plan.

There is a specific requirement for the AGC to support individual Goalkeepers across the Foundation Phase by delivering on the agreed commitments within each players Individual Learning Plan (ILP) and leading the process of continual review and refinement supporting the programme to be suitably responsive to each individual’s dynamic needs. 

This essentially makes the AGC responsible for the following, non-exhaustive list:
Preparing
  • Support the Lead Schoolboy Academy Goalkeeper Coach, and where necessary lead, with the creation and ongoing development of the Individual Learning Plans for all Foundation Phase Goalkeepers. 
  • Plan and prepare engaging goalkeeping sessions that aid individual player development in an integrated fashion with a specific focus on goalkeeping techniques. 
  • Prepare honest, thoughtful and impactful content for Individual Player Reviews and Parent Reviews. 
  • Liaise with age group coaches to ensure clear communication on the Goalkeeping Programme. 
  • Proactively engage within age group multi-disciplinary teams (‘MDT’) to provide the best possible support for each individual Goalkeeper. 
  • Provide advanced and consistent communication on programme logistics via the Clubs communication app (Teamworks) to players & parents.

Coaching
  • Lead the delivery of the Academy Goalkeeper Coaching Programme across the Foundation Phase. 
  • Support Academy Goalkeepers on Match days with purposeful pre-match and in-game Coaching. 
  • Contribute to the ongoing development of the Foundation Phase Goalkeeper Curriculum. 
  • Deliver sessions that stretch and challenge the clubs Foundation Phase Goalkeepers whilst continuing to develop their love and passion for the role of the Goalkeeper.
  • Proactively support Foundation Phase Goalkeepers within team training sessions. 
  • Assist and support Goalkeeper coaching sessions across the pathway, as and when required. 
  • Contribute to Talent Identification processes and evenings across the season, as and when required.

Reviewing
  • Systematically log and record training sessions via the Football Intelligence Platform (Kitman Labs). 
  • Support the Lead Schoolboy Goalkeeper Coach with honest and meaningful feedback, on player performance and progression, within Player Review Meetings and Parent Review Meetings. 
  • Contribute proactively to Goalkeeper Department meetings and Goalkeeper MDT meetings. 
  • Reflect on, and review, individual player performance and potential, to aid the decision-making process within Succession Planning meetings.

Benefits

We expect to close applications on Friday 2nd October, but if we receive a high level of interest, we may close the vacancy sooner. To avoid disappointment, please submit your application at the earliest opportunity.

job.title: Operations Manager - Fulham Pier
job.html_description:
Position Purpose 
​
The Operations Manager will support the Head of Building Services in the day-to-day operation of Fulham Pier, providing a visible management presence across the venue and ensuring that the building operates effectively and to the required standard.
The role will work closely with Building Services, Security, Cleaning, Hospitality, Events and the various operators across Fulham Pier, taking ownership of operational issues and ensuring they are resolved or appropriately escalated.
The role is operational rather than technical. It is specifically intended to provide management coverage across Fulham Pier's core operating hours and will routinely include evening and weekend working.

Responsibilities


Knowledge, Skills & Experience
  • Experience in an operational management, facilities, venue, hospitality or similar environment.
  • Experience of working in a busy public-facing operation.
  • Strong organisational skills with a practical and proactive approach to problem solving.
  • Experience working with contractors and service providers.
  • High standards and strong attention to detail.
  • Good communication skills and the confidence to deal with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently, make sensible operational decisions and know when to escalate.
  • Experience of purchasing, budget management or invoice approval.
  • Good IT skills.

Experience within a hospitality, hotel, leisure, sporting, entertainment or mixed-use venue, together with facilities, health and safety or licensing experience, would be advantageous.
 
Personal Attributes

The successful candidate will be visible, hands-on and comfortable taking ownership of issues. They will have high standards, good judgement and a practical approach to problem solving, and will be comfortable challenging poor standards where necessary.
They will understand that Fulham Pier is a seven-day operation and be flexible in their approach to working evenings and weekends.

Requirements


Operations & Standards
  • Provide a visible, hands-on management presence across Fulham Pier.
  • Regularly inspect public, guest and back-of-house areas and maintain high standards of presentation, cleanliness and operation.
  • Identify and resolve operational issues, ensuring outstanding matters are followed through.
  • Act as a key operational point of contact when the Head of Building Services is not on site.
  • Work with the different teams and operators across the Pier to coordinate activity and resolve issues.
  • Support events and periods of increased activity and ensure effective operational handovers.
  • Monitor the performance of cleaning, security, maintenance and other service providers and address deficiencies where required.
Building Services & Maintenance
  • Support the coordination of planned and reactive maintenance across Fulham Pier.
  • Ensure faults and defects are reported, prioritised and progressed.
  • Liaise with contractors, coordinate access and monitor the completion and quality of works.
  • Develop a good working knowledge of the building and its services, escalating technical matters to the appropriate specialist or contractor.
Licensing, Planning & Noise
  • Support the operation of Fulham Pier in accordance with its premises licences, planning permissions and agreed operating procedures.
  • Maintain a working knowledge of the key conditions affecting operating hours, external areas, events and noise.
  • Monitor compliance while on duty and take appropriate action where issues arise.
  • Monitor noise and activity, particularly during evenings and events, and ensure agreed noise management measures are followed.
  • Respond to operational or noise complaints while on duty, ensuring appropriate action is taken and recorded.
  • Escalate significant or recurring compliance issues to the Head of Building Services and relevant Club management.
Safety
  • Support the maintenance of a safe environment for staff, guests, contractors and visitors.
  • Identify hazards and operational risks and ensure appropriate action is taken.
  • Support emergency and incident procedures as required.
  • Ensure relevant inspections, incidents and actions are appropriately recorded.
Procurement & Financial Administration
  • Procure goods, services and minor works required for the operation of Fulham Pier within agreed procedures and delegated authority.
  • Obtain quotations, raise purchase orders and liaise directly with suppliers and contractors.
  • Review and approve invoices within delegated authority, confirming satisfactory delivery or completion of works.
  • Support the Head of Building Services in monitoring operational expenditure and achieving value for money.

Working Hours

Fulham Pier operates throughout the day, evenings and weekends. The Operations Manager will work flexibly to provide management coverage across these periods.
Regular evening and weekend working is a normal requirement of the role and will form part of the individual's standard working pattern.

job.title: Foundation Safeguarding Manager
job.html_description:
In this role, we’re looking for someone with clear vision and depth of knowledge to support Fulham Football Club Foundation in achieving the objectives of the safeguarding strategy. Someone who will make positive changes that are felt across the Foundation and football industry. To do that, you’ll be well versed in safeguarding best practice, which you’ll then communicate with credibility to the Foundation workforce. 

The post will be responsible for the oversight and direct provision of all safeguarding activities and associated training across the foundation. It is key that there is a Foundation-wide awareness of current football regulations and safeguarding best practice in respect of safeguarding whilst promoting a culture of equality and inclusion. The successful candidate will also be an active advocate of safeguarding for the Foundation internally and externally.


Responsibilities

•  Conduct regular observations of activity and site visits which include working irregular hours, such as evening and some weekends ensuring that safeguarding practices are embedded in delivery.  
•  To support the Head of Safeguarding, ensuring the Foundation and its staff are fully compliant with all safeguarding legislation, Premier League, EFL and FA guidance and to embed safeguarding into the culture of the Foundation. 
•  Work closely with both the Safeguarding and Equality Diversity and Inclusion leads to ensure the Foundation is providing a safe and inclusive environment.
•  Ensure that new staff/ volunteers are embedding safeguarding practices in delivery during induction period 
•  Oversee and develop the Quality Assurance provision in partnership with the Head of Safeguarding and Director of Operations, focusing on the high-risk areas of the Foundation’s delivery to ensure that front line staff are equipped to put safeguarding at the forefront of their delivery and responsibilities. 
•  To support programme leads with the running of Youth Voice, to ensure that children and young people and vulnerable adults are heard and their views on safeguarding and latest trends are taken into account. 
•  Address concerns reported on the Foundations safeguarding reporting system, CPOMS. Lead monthly meetings with senior leaders to review reports. 
•  Support the Head of Safeguarding with the incident and near miss reporting process across the Foundation ensuring thorough investigations are carried out and escalated through appropriate channels.
•  Using CPOMS, track data in relation to incidents, accidents and complaints, identify patterns and trends to inform organisational direction. Act as lead Foundation official and lead on or support the Head of Safeguarding in any investigation of an allegation of abuse or poor practice.
•  Work closely with the Foundation’s participants, coaches and staff (operations, programmes, training, observations)
•  Oversight of safeguarding recording on CPOMS including the monitoring, analysis and evaluation.
•  To work with the Head of Safeguarding and HR to ensure that all staff/volunteers who are working with children and young people are DBS checked and attend a safeguarding induction and regular safeguarding workshops. 
•  Work closely with HR to ensure that the single central record for each activity at the Foundation that involves Children and/or Adults at Risk is maintained, including relevant and permitted Disclosure information, safeguarding training records and any other information relevant to Safeguarding Vulnerable Groups. 
•  Conduct regular spot check audits throughout the year to assess compliance with safeguarding standards. 
•  Provide advice and guidance to the HR Department (and other departments as required) on all safeguarding related legislation.
•  Support staff in the sign-off process of planning off-site activities, trips, residentials and events.
•  Ensure that all third parties and partners that the Foundation engage with are compliant with safeguarding legislation and league standards. 
•  Ensure sensitive information is held securely, is GDPR compliant and all safeguarding and wellbeing concerns are recorded on our electronic case management system. 
•  Contribute to successful relationships with the English Football League, Premier League, FA and support other collaborations with agencies such as schools, education, social services, the Police and Youth Offending Teams. 
•  To advise on Foundation external activities including match day activities in relation to safeguarding.
•  To lead on keeping the organisation up to date and in line with legislation and communications around policies and processes associated with safeguarding activity.
•  To support the Head of Safeguarding and Director of Safeguarding and Inclusion to ensure the Foundation reaches its potential on all relevant safeguarding audits and be accountable for audit recommendations being monitored, reviewed and implemented. 
•  Provide relevant advice and guidance and embed best practice as appropriate.
•  Execute additional tasks as required in order to meet the Foundation’s changing priorities.
•  Champion and provide a vocal presence for Mental Health & Wellbeing within the Foundation;
•  Attend Mental Health & Wellbeing related working groups/action groups and offer operational perspective as and when required, and share information and communicate progress/issues back to colleagues;
•  Attend Foundation forums to share information and promote the safety of young people;
•  Work respectfully, sensitively and empathically with people with poor mental health and/or illness at all times;
•  Support any requests for updates on activities undertaken by the organisation around mental health.


Requirements

Essential
Experience:
•  Experience in social work, teaching or a related field working with children and/or adults at risk. Must have a background/experience in safeguarding preferably in a youth setting.
•  Recent experience of working effectively with external agencies, local community and a governing body.
•  Experienced in managing safeguarding concerns and keeping clear and comprehensive records of incidents.
•  Ability to contribute to the implementation and regular updating of policies and procedures for the safeguarding of children and ‘adults at risk’ across all areas of the club.

Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
Knowledge of:
•  The current safeguarding challenges in football/sport.
•  The UK safeguarding best practice.

Skills
•  Exceptional communication skills – both oral and written (presentation skills and delivery of ideas)
•  Commitment to collaborative and consultative working.
•  An understanding of the importance of, and the desire to engage with and inspire young people whatever their challenges.
•  The ability to deal sensitively with complex problems that can arise in child protection issues and/or similar matters.
•  A proven ability to manage change and to establish and maintain good working relationships with staff, children, young people, parents and ‘adults at risk’ – ability to work well with others is vital.
•  Experience of providing training and development for staff.
•  Excellent organisational skills, ability to effectively manage competing priorities and adhere to a range of tight deadlines.
•  High degree of professionalism and integrity, who will uphold the values of the Foundation. 

Qualifications
  • Relevant safeguarding qualification - appropriate experience will be accepted as an alternative.
  • Evidence of on-going CPD.

Desirable
Experience:
  • A track record in overseeing safeguarding arrangements for ‘adults at risk.’

Knowledge of:
•  The impact of EDI on Safeguarding practices.
•  ‘Prevent’ including extremist and terrorist groups. 
•  Safeguarding, safer recruitment and equality and diversity practice.

Skills
•  Working in a similar role, ideally in a governing or membership body within sport or other suitable industry.
•  Demonstrable experience of strategies to raise standards; an aptitude and enthusiasm for effective analysis of data and its use in setting targets for improvement.

Qualifications
•  Degree or equivalent level qualification or experience.
job.plain_text_description:
In this role, we’re looking for someone with clear vision and depth of knowledge to support Fulham Football Club Foundation in achieving the objectives of the safeguarding strategy. Someone who will make positive changes that are felt across the Foundation and football industry. To do that, you’ll be well versed in safeguarding best practice, which you’ll then communicate with credibility to the Foundation workforce.
The post will be responsible for the oversight and direct provision of all safeguarding activities and associated training across the foundation. It is key that there is a Foundation-wide awareness of current football regulations and safeguarding best practice in respect of safeguarding whilst promoting a culture of equality and inclusion. The successful candidate will also be an active advocate of safeguarding for the Foundation internally and externally.
Responsibilities
• Conduct regular observations of activity and site visits which include working irregular hours, such as evening and some weekends ensuring that safeguarding practices are embedded in delivery.
• To support the Head of Safeguarding, ensuring the Foundation and its staff are fully compliant with all safeguarding legislation, Premier League, EFL and FA guidance and to embed safeguarding into the culture of the Foundation.
• Work closely with both the Safeguarding and Equality Diversity and Inclusion leads to ensure the Foundation is providing a safe and inclusive environment.
• Ensure that new staff/ volunteers are embedding safeguarding practices in delivery during induction period
• Oversee and develop the Quality Assurance provision in partnership with the Head of Safeguarding and Director of Operations, focusing on the high-risk areas of the Foundation’s delivery to ensure that front line staff are equipped to put safeguarding at the forefront of their delivery and responsibilities.
• To support programme leads with the running of Youth Voice, to ensure that children and young people and vulnerable adults are heard and their views on safeguarding and latest trends are taken into account.
• Address concerns reported on the Foundations safeguarding reporting system, CPOMS. Lead monthly meetings with senior leaders to review reports.
• Support the Head of Safeguarding with the incident and near miss reporting process across the Foundation ensuring thorough investigations are carried out and escalated through appropriate channels.
• Using CPOMS, track data in relation to incidents, accidents and complaints, identify patterns and trends to inform organisational direction. Act as lead Foundation official and lead on or support the Head of Safeguarding in any investigation of an allegation of abuse or poor practice.
• Work closely with the Foundation’s participants, coaches and staff (operations, programmes, training, observations)
• Oversight of safeguarding recording on CPOMS including the monitoring, analysis and evaluation.
• To work with the Head of Safeguarding and HR to ensure that all staff/volunteers who are working with children and young people are DBS checked and attend a safeguarding induction and regular safeguarding workshops.
• Work closely with HR to ensure that the single central record for each activity at the Foundation that involves Children and/or Adults at Risk is maintained, including relevant and permitted Disclosure information, safeguarding training records and any other information relevant to Safeguarding Vulnerable Groups.
• Conduct regular spot check audits throughout the year to assess compliance with safeguarding standards.
• Provide advice and guidance to the HR Department (and other departments as required) on all safeguarding related legislation.
• Support staff in the sign-off process of planning off-site activities, trips, residentials and events.
• Ensure that all third parties and partners that the Foundation engage with are compliant with safeguarding legislation and league standards.
• Ensure sensitive information is held securely, is GDPR compliant and all safeguarding and wellbeing concerns are recorded on our electronic case management system.
• Contribute to successful relationships with the English Football League, Premier League, FA and support other collaborations with agencies such as schools, education, social services, the Police and Youth Offending Teams.
• To advise on Foundation external activities including match day activities in relation to safeguarding.
• To lead on keeping the organisation up to date and in line with legislation and communications around policies and processes associated with safeguarding activity.

• Execute additional tasks as required in order to meet the Foundation’s changing priorities.

• Attend Mental Health & Wellbeing related working groups/action groups and offer operational perspective as and when required, and share information and communicate progress/issues back to colleagues;

job.title: Matchday Groundsperson Casual
job.html_description:
The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:

• Repair works to the pitch in the form of divoting after warm up’s, half time and post-match use.
• Post-match pedestrian mowing using rotary and cylinder mowers.
• Setting up grow lights and moving them from storage compound into stadium post-game when required.
• Washing and cleaning of machinery after usage.
• Comply with all Health and Safety regulations and requirements within the Company and your role.
• Drive vehicles and handle equipment as required for grounds maintenance operations.
• Establish and maintain effective working relationships with managers, colleagues and end users, ensure grounds management are kept informed of any issues that may be identified.
• Undertaking general maintenance operations associated with pitch.
• Work within a stadium team to ensure the upkeep of the stadium pitch.
• This job description does not contain all the duties and responsibilities that may arise in this role, you will need to undertake other duties as instructed and use initiative to ensure the safe operational functioning of the stadium.
• Expectation is to work at least 75% of home fixtures.

job.title: Hospitality Ticketing Executive (Casual)
job.html_description:
As a Hospitality Ticketing Executive (Casual Matchday Role), you will play an important part in delivering an exceptional experience for guests attending Fulham Football Club on matchdays.

This is a casual position, with shifts available on home matchdays and selected event days only. The role offers flexible, ad hoc work and is ideal for individuals looking for occasional employment in a fast-paced sporting environment.

Working from the Hospitality Ticket Office, you will predominantly support hospitality guests while also acting as the first point of matchday support for guests attending through the Club's Authorised Resellers and Group Bookings. From ticketing enquiries and digital ticket support to stadium access and general matchday assistance, you will help ensure every guest receives a friendly, professional and welcoming service from arrival through to kick-off.

Working closely with the Hospitality Sales, Service, Ticketing, Matchday Operations and Security teams, you will help create a smooth and enjoyable experience for every guest visiting Craven Cottage on matchdays.

Responsibilities

  • Welcome hospitality guests, Authorised Reseller guests and Group Booking guests in a friendly, professional and approachable manner
  • Provide first-line support for ticketing enquiries, digital ticket issues, stadium access and general matchday queries
  • Assist with ticket collection, ticket reprints and resolving straightforward ticketing and access issues
  • Support guests attending through the Club's Authorised Resellers, including both Hospitality and General Admission bookings
  • Support Group Booking guests with ticketing enquiries, stadium access and general matchday assistance
  • Resolve standard ticketing and matchday queries, escalating more complex issues where appropriate
  • Direct General Admission enquiries not relating to Authorised Reseller or Group Bookings to the Club's Ticket Office
  • Provide accurate information on hospitality experiences, seating locations, stadium access and matchday operations
  • Work collaboratively with Hospitality Sales, Service, Ticketing, Matchday Operations and Security teams to deliver an exceptional guest experience
  • Follow Club procedures when handling tickets and guest information, maintaining the highest standards of professionalism, accuracy and confidentiality
  • Carry out any other reasonable duties required to support the successful delivery of the Club's hospitality and matchday ticketing operation

Requirements

Essential Skills & Experience
The Hospitality Ticketing Executive (Casual) must have:
  • Excellent customer service skills
  • A friendly, confident and professional manner
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • Good attention to detail
  • Confidence using computer systems and digital ticketing platforms
  • The ability to remain calm, organised and solution-focused in a busy environment
  • A positive, proactive and team-focused approach
  • Reliability, punctuality and a willingness to learn
  • Flexibility to work evenings, weekends and all home first-team fixtures

Desirable Skills & Experience
Ideally, the Hospitality Ticketing Executive (Casual) will have:
  • Previous customer service experience
  • Experience working within hospitality, retail, sport or live events
  • Experience using ticketing or booking systems
  • An interest in football and live events

job.title: Host Family
job.html_description:
Are you passionate about football and looking for a unique opportunity to make a difference in the lives of young athletes, aged 15-21?


Fulham FC is seeking warm and welcoming host families to provide a safe and supportive home environment to support our Academy players who will be required to live away from home to fulfil their education and football training at our club.


As a host parent, you will play an essential role in helping our players thrive both on and off the pitch. You'll provide a comfortable living space, home-cooked meals, emotional support and help them to adjust to life away from home as they focus on their training and academic pursuits.


What we are looking for:
  • A friendly, caring family or individual with a spare room
  • A willingness to provide support, guidance, and encouragement to our young players
  • A safe and welcoming home environment
  • Support our young people by teaching them basic independent living and self-care skills such as washing, cooking and cleaning up after themselves.
  • Providing meals in line with nutritional guidance from the Academy.
  • Accommodation has access to public and local amenities with good transport links to the Academy training ground.
  • Report any welfare concerns to the Academy Safeguarding and Player Care team should they occur.
  • Include our young people in family life as much as they feel comfortable with.
  • The club will regularly inspect and visit the placement during the season.
  • The club will provide further guidance to host families, young people and their parents explaining what would be expected of them.

In order to be considered for this position you must live within 30 minutes travel for the player from the training ground.

Fulham Football Club is committed to safeguarding and ensuring the welfare and protection of children and young people and expects host families to share this commitment. As such, the host family provider will be subject to an Enhanced Disclosure & Barring Service (DBS) check and risk assessments prior to a placement commencing.


Any other person over the age of 18, who resides in the household or has regular contact with the player will be required to complete an enhanced DBS. Host Families will be required to attend safeguarding training and workshops arranged by the Academy.


We are committed to supporting an environment where all staff have a personal responsibility to uphold the Club’s Equal Opportunities Policy by treating fellow employees, prospective employees, casual workers, prospective casual workers, players, prospective players and customers fairly and impartially.

job.title: Maintenance Engineer - Electrician
job.html_description:
We are looking for an experienced Electrician to provide a comprehensive high standard of Maintenance support to the Club and proactively identify areas for improvement and develop and implement solutions.

Responsibilities

The Maintenance Engineer – Electrician must: 
  • Experience of electrical installation within a large commercial environment 
  • NVQ level 1, 2, 3 in Electrical Installation
  • 18th Edition

Ideally, Maintenance Engineer – Electrician will: 
  • Experience in previous Maintenance roles
  • Experience using Planned Maintenance software 
  • Full Driving Licence
  • PAT testing experience
  • Proven ability to work unsupervised and as part of a team
  • Proactive
  • Organised
  • Flexible Attitude
  • Team Player 

Requirements

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role: 
  • To carry out electrical work, both reactive and planned maintenance
  • To carry out general day to day maintenance duties, which will sometimes be on very tight deadlines and to a high-level finish
  • General planned maintenance is divided between the team dependant on site coverage
  • Site electrical installations and upgrade works
  • Assist in ad-hoc projects where required
  • Matchday preparation carried out 24-72hrs prior to each game
  • Matchday & Event cover along with other team members
  • To ensure that all work is carried out in a safe manner and within relevant Health and Safety Guidelines
  • Covering Events where required 

Benefits

Applications close on 21st August.

job.title: Casual Football & Sports Coach - Development Centres
job.html_description:
To deliver high quality football coaching sessions to accomplished & aspiring grassroots players aged 6 to 16.

To deliver football & sports sessions across the wider Foundation to a range of children, young people and adults.


Responsibilities

  • To act as an Ambassador for FFCF and maintain and develop relationships to ensure high quality experiences for young people, partner organisations, other staff and customers

  • To effectively plan and deliver high quality football sessions in-line with coaching syllabus, philosophy and values

  • To effectively support the development of individual players through the creation of individual development plans throughout the season

  • To identify and support the development of progression pathways for talented young people

  • To effectively plan and deliver extra-curricular and community activities across the wider Foundation

  • To support the transition between school-based activities, wider Foundation activities and where appropriate, other community activities

  • Assist in data collection and completion of monitoring for reports on an ongoing basis, within the timescales required

  • To work closely with Football Development Officer's to understand programme standards and attendance targets and support the promotion of FFCF activities

  • To support the smooth function of the Operations Department in line with the Foundation values and targets and work across programmes, when required

Requirements

Essential:

Experience:
  • Leading football sessions to age groups U7 to U16
  • Delivery of extracurricular and community activities to all age groups
  • Supporting and developing coaches in a sports environment
  • Working with external partners to achieve successful outcome
  • Monitoring and Evaluation 
  • Marketing and promotion

Skills, knowledge & qualifications:
  • Minimum of UEFA C qualification in Coaching Football
  • FA First Aid - in date
  • FA Safeguarding - in date
  • Ability to drive, has access to a car or ability to travel independently

Personal qualities:
  • Committed and motivated by the purpose of the Foundation 
  • Demonstrates respect for colleagues, partners and customers and when possible operates above and beyond expectations
  • Well presented with a good manner
  • Excellent punctuality
  • Ability to prioritise work and consistently meet deadlines
  • Effective communicator
  • Cheerful positive attitude

Preferred:

Experience:
  • Delivery in a Club Community Organisation (CCO)
  • Delivery of activiry to young people with a Disability. 
  • Delivery of CPD events to coaches.
  • Delivery of Physical Education lessons to primary age children

Skills, knowledge ​& qualifications:
  • UEFA B qualification
  • Non-football NGB sports qualifications
  • Mentoring qualification
  • Talent Identification qualification
  • Understanding of Physical Education standards in schools (Ofsted guidance)

job.title: FP Head Coach
job.html_description:
The Foundation Phase Head Coach Coach is responsible for leading the coaching programme for a designated age group, ensuring that all coaching, player development, and staff support activities are delivered in line with the Academy Performance Plan and the club's playing philosophy. The role will provide leadership and direction to coaches and support staff, creating a high-performance environment that maximises the development of Academy players both on and off the pitch.

The postholder will plan, prepare, deliver, and review high-quality coaching sessions and matchday activities, ensuring a consistent approach to player development that reflects the Academy's technical, tactical, physical, psychological, and social objectives. They will monitor player progress, contribute to individual development planning, and work collaboratively with multidisciplinary staff to support each player's long-term growth and performance.

In addition, the role will play a key part in the ongoing development and implementation of the Academy Performance Plan, providing insights, feedback, and innovative ideas to support the continuous evolution of the Academy Technical Plan. The successful candidate will champion best practice in coaching, foster a positive and inclusive learning environment, and contribute to the achievement of the Academy's strategic objectives and long-term vision.

Responsibilities

The FP Head Coach must:  
  • Be player/person centred (individualised) in their approach to development. 
  • Have a strong understanding of coaching and player development principles, ensuring alignment in both beliefs and actions, with the Academy Performance Plan.
  • Have experience of working with (ideally coaching, teaching, educating or supporting) young people and parents in an Academy or Educational setting.
  • Hold appropriate and up to date qualifications to conform to Professional Game Academy Audit Company (PGAAC) and Premier League Youth Development Rules (PLYDR) requirements.
  • Remain up to date with the continual professional development requirements associated with all relevant licences held.
  • Have broad awareness of the football industry’s governing policies and youth football protocols, in particular all relevant aspects of the Premier Leagues Youth Development Rules.
  • Be diligent, hard-working, detail driven and (largely) intrinsically motivated by the Academy’s mission.
  • Hold a forward thinking, positive and optimistic mindset and nature.
  • Demonstrate and model high levels of professionalism in organisation, delivery and conduct.
  • Be able to continuously demonstrate openness, inclusiveness and a willingness to collaborate within everyday behaviours.
  • Show pro-activeness and be able to work around or overcome obstacles that others may find challenging.
  • Have knowledge of regulations and expected practices in relation to working with young people, with particular reference to safeguarding, well-being and safety.
  • Have high-level interpersonal skills, including being an effective and adaptable communicator.
  • Demonstrate resilience towards the everyday rigours of high-performance environments.
  • Be willing to hold honest and supportive conversations with parents, guardians or carers of Academy players.
  • Be highly motivated and passionate about supporting players (and staff) to achieve development outcomes.
  • Understand the importance of being a ‘confident custodian’ for an organisation with history and tradition.
 
Ideally, the FP Head Coach will:  
  • Hold the FA Talent Identification Level 1 qualification.
  • Hold a higher education degree in coaching, analysis or sports science (or similar qualification).

Requirements

Preparing (‘be detail orientated when it comes to planning and preparation’) 
  • Lead the creation and ongoing development of both Individual Learning Plans (‘ILP’) and the Age Group Plan.
  • Lead communication with players and families around the programme (training, fixtures and reviews).
  • Lead the MDT to prepare and integrate their work, creating team and individual training plans.
  • Lead the preparation of meaningful content for individual player reviews.
  • Support the preparation of content for team and individual performance education delivery.
 
Delivering (‘be a uniquely outstanding deliverer to Academy players’) 
  • Lead the delivery of team training sessions in line with the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (Technical Plan (‘TP’)) specifically integrating team and individual outcomes into practice.
  • Lead the delivery of individual training sessions (both inside and outside of team training sessions) in line with ILP commitments.
  • Lead teams and individuals through fixtures, tours and tournaments, aligning the environment design and coaching behaviours to the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (TP).
  • Lead the delivery of performance education sessions in line with the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (TP).
 
Reviewing (‘understanding that we develop through and from our everyday experiences)  
  • Lead the effective review of team training sessions in line with ‘reflection’ expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (TP).
  • Lead the effective review of individual training sessions and their impact on player-coach relationships and player performance over time.
  • Coordinate the review of team and individuals match performances in all games programme, tours and tournament fixtures.
  • Coordinate the ongoing ‘rolling’ review of each players ILP, ensuring the creation of clear action plans, involving colleagues from different disciplinary backgrounds, through weekly MDT meetings.
  • Record reflections on personal coaching performance (in both training and fixture environments) in line with the ‘reflection’ expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (TP).
  • Lead the effective review of player review events and processes, ensuring improvements are actioned over time.
  • Support the effective review of the performance education programme for the age group.

Benefits

We expect to close applications on 21st September, but if we receive a high level of interest, we may close the vacancy sooner. To avoid disappointment, please submit your application at the earliest opportunity.
job.plain_text_description:
The Foundation Phase Head Coach Coach is responsible for leading the coaching programme for a designated age group, ensuring that all coaching, player development, and staff support activities are delivered in line with the Academy Performance Plan and the club's playing philosophy. The role will provide leadership and direction to coaches and support staff, creating a high-performance environment that maximises the development of Academy players both on and off the pitch.
The postholder will plan, prepare, deliver, and review high-quality coaching sessions and matchday activities, ensuring a consistent approach to player development that reflects the Academy's technical, tactical, physical, psychological, and social objectives. They will monitor player progress, contribute to individual development planning, and work collaboratively with multidisciplinary staff to support each player's long-term growth and performance.
In addition, the role will play a key part in the ongoing development and implementation of the Academy Performance Plan, providing insights, feedback, and innovative ideas to support the continuous evolution of the Academy Technical Plan. The successful candidate will champion best practice in coaching, foster a positive and inclusive learning environment, and contribute to the achievement of the Academy's strategic objectives and long-term vision.
Responsibilities
The FP Head Coach must:
- Be player/person centred (individualised) in their approach to development. - Have a strong understanding of coaching and player development principles, ensuring alignment in both beliefs and actions, with the Academy Performance Plan. - Have experience of working with (ideally coaching, teaching, educating or supporting) young people and parents in an Academy or Educational setting. - Hold appropriate and up to date qualifications to conform to Professional Game Academy Audit Company (PGAAC) and Premier League Youth Development Rules (PLYDR) requirements. - Remain up to date with the continual professional development requirements associated with all relevant licences held. - Have broad awareness of the football industry’s governing policies and youth football protocols, in particular all relevant aspects of the Premier Leagues Youth Development Rules. - Be diligent, hard-working, detail driven and (largely) intrinsically motivated by the Academy’s mission. - Hold a forward thinking, positive and optimistic mindset and nature. - Demonstrate and model high levels of professionalism in organisation, delivery and conduct. - Be able to continuously demonstrate openness, inclusiveness and a willingness to collaborate within everyday behaviours. - Show pro-activeness and be able to work around or overcome obstacles that others may find challenging. - Have knowledge of regulations and expected practices in relation to working with young people, with particular reference to safeguarding, well-being and safety. - Have high-level interpersonal skills, including being an effective and adaptable communicator. - Demonstrate resilience towards the everyday rigours of high-performance environments. - Be willing to hold honest and supportive conversations with parents, guardians or carers of Academy players. - Be highly motivated and passionate about supporting players (and staff) to achieve development outcomes. - Understand the importance of being a ‘confident custodian’ for an organisation with history and tradition.
Ideally, the FP Head Coach will:
- Hold the FA Talent Identification Level 1 qualification. - Hold a higher education degree in coaching, analysis or sports science (or similar qualification).
Requirements
Preparing (‘be detail orientated when it comes to planning and preparation’)
- Lead the creation and ongoing development of both Individual Learning Plans (‘ILP’) and the Age Group Plan. - Lead communication with players and families around the programme (training, fixtures and reviews). - Lead the MDT to prepare and integrate their work, creating team and individual training plans. - Lead the preparation of meaningful content for individual player reviews. - Support the preparation of content for team and individual performance education delivery.
Delivering (‘be a uniquely outstanding deliverer to Academy players’)
- Lead the delivery of team training sessions in line with the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (Technical Plan (‘TP’)) specifically integrating team and individual outcomes into practice. - Lead the delivery of individual training sessions (both inside and outside of team training sessions) in line with ILP commitments. - Lead teams and individuals through fixtures, tours and tournaments, aligning the environment design and coaching behaviours to the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (TP). - Lead the delivery of performance education sessions in line with the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (TP).
Reviewing (‘understanding that we develop through and from our everyday experiences)
- Lead the effective review of team training sessions in line with ‘reflection’ expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (TP). - Lead the effective review of individual training sessions and their impact on player-coach relationships and player performance over time. - Coordinate the review of team and individuals match performances in all games programme, tours and tournament fixtures. - Coordinate the ongoing ‘rolling’ review of each players ILP, ensuring the creation of clear action plans, involving colleagues from different disciplinary backgrounds, through weekly MDT meetings. - Record reflections on personal coaching performance (in both training and fixture environments) in line with the ‘reflection’ expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (TP). - Lead the effective review of player review events and processes, ensuring improvements are actioned over time. - Support the effective review of the performance education programme for the age group.
Benefits
We expect to close applications on 21st September, but if we receive a high level of interest, we may close the vacancy sooner. To avoid disappointment, please submit your application at the earliest opportunity.

job.title: Stadium Tour Guide - Weekend
job.html_description:
We intend on building the Craven Cottage stadium tour to be one of the truly popular London experiences for football fans and visitors to London. Our guides are key to this objective. 
Craven Cottage tour guides are expected to be hard working, well presented, passionate and dedicated to ensuring that our guest’s expectations are met every time. Guides are also expected to be proactive and receptive to performance feedback and to be enthusiastic, proud club ambassadors in every possible aspect of the position.

Responsibilities

PERSON SPECIFICATION AND ATTRIBUTES
 
  • Smart and well presented
  • Guest oriented
  • Positive attitude
  • Friendly, flexible and proactive
  • Strong team player with the ability and willingness to work alone
  • Knowledgeable and passionate regarding Craven Cottage and Fulham Football Club
  • Willing to improve and develop
  • Reliable and punctual
  • High personal standards
  • Values and respects others
  • Takes responsibility
  • Ideally a Fulham fan but this is not essential
  • The ability and willingness to work home match days if required
  • The willingness to wear official club branded clothes as directed by the stadium   tour manager when leading tours or on duty.
  • The ability to regularly work weekends


Skills and Experience
 
  • Excellent communication skills with  the confidence to speak to large groups
  • Customer service skills with the desire to improve
  • The ability to study and learn the history of the club and ground
  • The ability to present the information to the timings required in an interesting, passionate manner and with   historical accuracy
  • The ability and interest in remaining up to date with the latest club news
  • Where necessary, the willingness and ability to work in an office environment, responding to emails, answering enquiries, selling tickets for the tour and tour events.

Requirements

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • To support the delivery of the Craven Cottage stadium tour, across all   operations and in every respect
  • To deliver an engaging stadium tour to a wide variety of guests
  • To handle payments
  • Provide a customer service experience to our guests that meets their expectations
  • To deliver a personable tour, including welcoming and saying goodbye to the   group
  • To deal with a wide variety of customer enquiries
  • To be a proud and enthusiastic club ambassador
  • Taking photo’s where requested for guests where and when permitted
  • To liase with stadium management, stadium tour manager and security on a tour   day and while the tour is in progress where necessary
  • Ensure that the tour route is litter free, clear, safe and adheres to health and   safety policies and procedures
  • To promote the club at every opportunity including ticketing, retail,   hospitality and events
  • Deliver other tours relevant to Fulham Football Club
  • To carry out other related duties that may reasonably be required including   covering for absent staff during holidays and sickness
  • To be responsible for the safety and security of staff, visitors and the ground   throughout the tour and while guests are present in the stadium. This   includes following instructions from the stadium tour manager, security,   stadium management and other departments

Benefits

Full training will be provided to the successful applicant.

This is a casual position and hours will be arranged accordingly.

Shifts will involve weekend, weekdays, bank holidays and potentially match days. Hours might involve evening shifts or early starts when required. The length of the shift may vary according to the needs of the organisation and events.

job.title: Academy Therapist (Casual)
job.html_description:
To deliver high-quality physiotherapy services across the Foundation Phase (FP) and Youth Development Phase (YDP) squads (U9–U16) within a multidisciplinary team environment. Provide medical support on match days, during clinics, and at tournaments, ensuring optimal care and performance outcomes for academy players. Assist in the implementation of injury prevention strategies and rehabilitation programmes aimed at maximising performance, enhancing recovery, and minimising injury risk. Support the effective transition of players from the FP and YDP into the Professional Development Phase (PDP) by contributing to a comprehensive and cohesive medical pathway.

Responsibilities

The therapist will play a key role in the delivery of medical services to academy players across the Foundation and Youth Development Phases. Working as part of a multidisciplinary team, they will support all aspects of injury management, contribute to player development through preventative care strategies, and ensure effective communication and documentation across all stakeholders.

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:
 • Provide medical cover for FP and YDP players during match days (primarily Sundays, with some midweek fixtures), evening clinics, and domestic or international tournaments. 
  • Support the assessment, treatment, and rehabilitation of injuries in collaboration with the full-time U9–U16 physiotherapist, ensuring appropriate return-to-play protocols are followed. 
  • Contribute to the planning and delivery of injury prevention strategies, including individual and group-based sessions tailored to player needs. 
  • Liaise effectively with coaching staff to support player load management during key stages of physical development. 
  • Communicate and coordinate with parents, external medical providers (NHS/private), and internal staff to facilitate appropriate ongoing care. 
  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date medical records on the PMA system and ensure clear handovers between staff for all FP and YDP players. 
  • Assist in the transition of players from FP/YDP into the PDP phase by sharing relevant medical and movement history with appropriate personnel. 
  • Engage in internal CPD, contribute to research and development within paediatric sports medicine, and undertake relevant professional development to support continuous improvement.

Requirements

The Casual Academy Therapist must:
  • BSc degree in Physiotherapy, Sports Therapy, Sports Rehabilitation. 
  • Be a member of the appropriate governing body – CSP, SST, BASRaT 
  • FA Level 4 ITMMiF • Experience working in a sports medicine environment.
  • Experience working in a multidisciplinary team. 
  • FA Safegurading • Be able to work as part of a team 
  • Available to work on a flexible basis including evening and weekends

Ideally, the Casual Academy Therapist will:
  • FA Level 5 ATMMiF
  • Experience and understanding of paediatric sports medicine 
  • Experience working within a Category 1 football academy

job.title: Warehouse Operative/Driver (Part-time)
job.plain_text_description:
Oversee the efficient receipt, storage, dispatch and movements of all stock. Be able to ensure productivity targets are achieved and that all warehouse processes are running smoothly and promptly. Delivering of Stock to the store.
This role is 24 hours per week: shifts on Monday, Tuesday and Friday.
Responsibilities
Below are example responsibilities but this is not intended to be an exhaustive list:
- Driving between sites to deliver retail stock as and when required. - Control retail stock movements - Responsible for pick, pack and dispatch in the online retail store. - Ensure product is stored in a safe and responsible manner. - Support Retail team in all aspects of stock and movements. - Support internet and online team. - Strategically manage warehouse in compliance with company’s policies and vision - Implement and adhere to all Club procedures ensuring all staff are fully aware and always trained - Uphold all retail security procedures, working closely with the Warehouse team - Support and reflect the Club Values on a day-to-day basis, ensuring the team are also demonstrating the appropriate behaviours - Proactively seek to build and maintain relationships with appropriate people in the business, and build the profile of the retail operation
Key Skills:
- A strong communication skill at all levels both oral and written - Strong interpersonal skills and confidence in dealing with people at all levels of the organisation - Pragmatic and flexible approach - Work well under pressure through very busy trading periods - Team player with a hands-on approach - Know how to do Shirt printings - The ability to drive a van for delivery purposes

Essential:
Experience:
· Retail Systems

job.title: Fire Officer
job.html_description:
Position Purpose 

 

The Fire Team will not normally be expected to be involved in the management of spectators. When deployed as a member of the Fire Team the primary is one of fire prevention and first response should an outbreak of fire occur.
This role is suitable for candidates who are or have experience of the fire industry or stewards who are willing to undergo additional fire safety training to enable them to carry out this role.

Responsibilities

  • Attend the Stadium at given dates and times as dictated by the Head of Safety.
  • Undertake pre-match and post-match fire checks as instructed by the Fire Team leader. Arrive at Steward Sign as directed.
  • Conduct Pre-Match Checks and specified documentation on Raven Controls as required.
  • Conduct patrols within the stand and under croft’s to minimise the risk of fire breaking out and assisting to prevent the spread of fire. 
  • Respond to Fire and associated incidents as directed by FFC Control, ensuring staff are supported, appropriate action is taken, and that information is passed to the Safety Management Team in FFC Control (Act – Inform – Escalate)
  • Attend during match meetings with Fire Team leader for the identification of issues to be addressed, learning points and review of specific deployments. 
  • Report any fire safety concerns to the fire team leader for appropriate action and escalation to FFC Control and the Safety Officer. 
  • Know the location of and be able to effectively operate the firefighting equipment at the Stadium. 
  • Be able to provide basic ‘First Aid’ if required. 
  • Know the location of the First Aid Rooms located within the Stadium. 
  • Be fully conversant with any methods or messages used to alert staff that an emergency has arisen. 
  • Be capable of recognising potential fire hazards and items of interest or suspect packages, reporting such matters immediately to the Fire Team leader, a Supervisor, Chief Steward, Deputy Safety Officer, or Safety Officer. 
  • Promptly comply with any instruction given by a Supervisor, Chief Steward, Deputy Safety Officer, Safety Officer, or Police Officer. 
  • Comply with the relevant instructions and guidance contained in the Stewards Handbook and standing instructions for the FFC Fire Team. 
  • Attend all required training. 
  • To understand their general responsibilities towards the health and safety and welfare of all spectators, other stewards, staff, and themselves.


Essential and Desirable 
 
Background in Fire industry (present/previous Fire Service) and willing to undergo relevant training. 

Requirements

To act in accordance with the general recommendations of the Guide to Safety at Sports Ground (Green Guide) and the specific requirements of the Safety Certificate issued by the Local Authority under the Safety of Sports Ground Act 1975. Fire Safety Officers play a key role in the event day safety team ensuring that the stadium provides a safe and secure environment for thousands of visitors. You will become a focal point for all fire safety issues, providing preventative advice and measures in an emergency.

 

  • You should be a minimum of 18 years of age, be fit, active and have the character and temperament to carry out the duties required. 
  • You should possess good communication skills.
  • You must be able to attend most first-team home fixtures and other major events held at the stadium.
  • You should be polite, courteous, and helpful to all supporters.
  • Whilst on duty you will adhere to the Club dress code and be clean and tidy.
  • You are not engaged to watch the game but are expected to concentrate on your area of responsibility. 
  • You should never show hostility or use obscene or offensive language to any supporters.
  • You should never act in any way likely to bring discredit on the Club.

job.title: Casual Football & Sports Coach - DisAbility
job.plain_text_description:
Fulham FC Foundation are currently seeking to recruit an enthusiastic and committed person to take up the casual position of DisAbility Football & Sports Coach.
Reporting directly to our Senior DisAbility Development Manager, the DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches are responsible for delivering high-quality football & sports coaching to children, young people and adults with disabilities and additional needs. This role involves delivery across a wide-range of our DisAbility Programmes, including Pan DisAbility Clubs, Active Autism, Down’s Syndrome ‘Badgers’, Blind and Partially Sighted, Cerebral Palsy and Dwarfism Football Sessions. In addition there will be opportunities to work in our DisAbility Schools programme delivering PE, Enrichment Activities and After School Clubs.
While the primary focus of this role is on DisAbility Football & Sport, there may be opportunities to contribute to other FFC Foundation activities such as Skills Club, Development Centres, Soccer Schools, Primary Education, Kicks, and Health & Wellbeing. We would encourage candidates to prioritise DisAbility Programmes where possible, while remaining flexible to support other areas as needed.
This is a casual role where flexibility is essential, as the role necessitates involvement in supporting the delivery of programme activities as and when required.
The successful candidate will be somebody who has prior experience delivering football & sports coaching sessions to children & young people with disabilities or additional needs in grassroots & school settings, holds at least a FA Level 1/Introduction to Coaching Football qualification and is committed to the charitable purpose of Fulham FC Foundation.
As this role is casual, there is no set timetable. Sessions may be offered on an adhoc or regular basis, depending on the needs of Fulham FC Foundation. It is the responsibility of the DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches to maintain consistent and effective communication with our Senior DisAbility Development Manager and Operations Officers to ensure the continuation of work.
Whilst there is no obligation for Fulham FC Foundation to provide, or for the DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches to accept, work. DisAbility Football & Sports Coaches who do not work for an extended period of time, will be deactivated.
The successful candidates should be available to work across at least one of the below times, in order to receive work. We are extremely keen to hear from those who are able to work on Saturday mornings.
Weekdays – 9am to 5 pm;
Weekday Evenings – 5pm to 9pm
Weekends – Saturdays – 8am to 12noon.
Work in other timings is available, however on a far reduced frequency.
Salary Range: £12.95 p/h to £16.50 p/h
Next steps
:
There is no closing date for this role. Applications will be reviewed on a bi-weekly basis.
If successful, you will join a vibrant team who are passionate about achieving the organisation's vision of “an active, inclusive and thriving community”, and you’ll have the opportunity to build on your existing skills through a variety of training and development opportunities and experiences
*
This job description should not be regarded as exclusive or exhaustive. It is intended as an outline indication of areas of activity and responsibility and will be amended in the light of the changing needs of the organisation
.
Responsibilities
- To act as an Ambassador for Fulham FC Foundation (FFCF), representing the organisation professionally in line with its values. - To plan and deliver high-quality football and sports coaching sessions to children, young people & adults in-line with FFCF standards. - To provide a safe, positive and inclusive learning environment at all times, - To adhere to FFCF’s safeguarding policies and procedures, ensuring the timely reporting of any safeguarding concerns or incidents within sessions. - To engage, include, inspire and grow participation across FFCF activities. - To support the transition of participants between different FFCF programmes and activities. - To champion opportunities for individuals from underrepresented groups within FFCF activities. - To identify and support progression pathways for talented young people. - To support the development of FFCF programmes through positive collaboration with Department Managers / Operations Officers. - To support the promotion of FFCF programmes across the local community. - To assist in data collection and completion of monitoring & evaluation on an ongoing basis.
Requirements
Essential:
Experience:
- Delivery of football coaching sessions in a grassroots environment - Delivery of sports coaching sessions to children, young people or adults with disabilities and additional needs. - Delivery within a school/college setting. - Working in a customer-facing role.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
- Introduction to Coaching Football qualification - In-date FA Emergency First Aid - In-date FA Safeguarding Children certificate - Base knowledge of and willingness to learn & contribute towards FFCF strategic aims.
Personal Qualities:
- A positive role-model for children & young people. - Ability to travel independently across South-West London, including transport of equipment. - Well presented, with a professional manner. - Positive, energetic persona. Able to build rapport with participants. - Excellent time-keeping & punctuality. - Willingness to learn & develop personally & professionally.
Preferred:
Experience:
- Delivery of football & sports coaching sessions in a Club Community Organisation (CCO). - Delivery of Physical Education within a school setting. - Delivery within a classroom environment. - Marketing & Promoting participation activities in the community. - Delivery of football & sports coaching sessions to females.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
- FA Level 2/UEFA C in Coaching Football qualification (or higher). - Additional PE/HLTA qualification - Mentoring qualification - Non-football NGB sports qualifications.

  • Available to work all home matchdays - weekends and evenings including bank holidays.
  • Adaptability to handle a variety of situations

Ideally, Matchday Retail Assistant will:
  • Previous EPOS experience
