• Provide excellent and helpful customer service, assisting customers with products and purchases.
• Operate the till and process card payments accurately.
• Print names and numbers onto replica shirts, ensuring customer orders are completed correctly and to a high standard.
• Replenish stock and keep stores and displays tidy and well-presented.
• Price and label products correctly across the store.
• Support the matchday running of the store and assist with additional tasks when required
• Work in various units across the stadium
job.plain_text_description:
Position Purpose
This role involves supporting the day-to-day operations of the Club’s retail store, delivering excellent customer service, maintaining high standards of presentation, and ensuring efficient stock handling and sales processes.
Responsibilities
Essential and Desirable
- Strong customer service and communication skills, with the ability to assist customers in a friendly and professional manner. - Able to work effectively in a fast-paced retail environment, both independently and as part of a team, while maintaining high standards of organisation and efficiency. - Available to work all home matchdays - weekends and evenings including bank holidays. - Adaptability to handle a variety of situations
Ideally, Matchday Retail Assistant will:
- Previous EPOS experience - Retail Experience
Requirements
The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:
• Provide excellent and helpful customer service, assisting customers with products and purchases.
• Operate the till and process card payments accurately.
• Print names and numbers onto replica shirts, ensuring customer orders are completed correctly and to a high standard.
• Replenish stock and keep stores and displays tidy and well-presented.
• Price and label products correctly across the store.
• Support the matchday running of the store and assist with additional tasks when required
• Work in various units across the stadium

job.title: Head of Grounds - Craven Cottage
job.html_description:
The Head of Grounds – Craven Cottage is responsible for the leadership, management, preparation and performance of the playing surface and associated grounds operations at Craven Cottage.
 
The postholder is accountable for ensuring that the stadium pitch is maintained and presented to the highest professional standards, providing a safe, consistent and high-performing playing surface for First Team, Women’s and Academy football, together with approved pitch hires, events and other stadium activity.
 
The role will develop and deliver annual pitch maintenance, renovation and improvement programmes, balancing a varied programme of football fixtures and training, commercial use, events, weather conditions and the long-term health and performance of the playing surface.
 
A key responsibility of the role is to manage and advise on pitch usage, working collaboratively with football and commercial stakeholders to maximise appropriate use of the stadium pitch whilst protecting playing quality, recovery periods and the Club’s long-term investment in the surface.
 
The postholder will lead the Craven Cottage grounds team, manage budgets, specialist machinery and pitch infrastructure, and work closely with Football Operations, Stadium Operations, Commercial and Events teams to ensure the playing surface is prepared to the required standard for all approved uses.

Responsibilities

Essential and Desirable
 
Essential Experience
  • Significant experience in professional sports turf management.
  • Experience in the preparation and maintenance of high-quality natural grass playing surfaces.
  • Experience operating within professional football, professional sport or a comparable elite sporting environment.
  • Experience managing playing surfaces subject to varied and intensive usage.
  • Experience leading and developing a grounds team.
  • Experience planning and delivering pitch maintenance and renovation programmes.
  • Experience managing budgets, contractors, machinery and operational resources.
  • Experience managing specialist pitch infrastructure including irrigation and drainage systems.

Essential Skills / Qualifications
  • Relevant qualification in Sports Turf, Horticulture or Grounds Management.
  • Strong technical knowledge of sports turf maintenance and agronomy.
  • Strong understanding of irrigation, drainage, turf machinery and pitch infrastructure.
  • Appropriate pesticide application qualifications relevant to the role.
  • Good working knowledge of Health & Safety requirements associated with grounds operations.
  • Good IT, administrative and record-keeping skills.
  • Strong organisational, planning and communication skills.
  • Ability to make sound operational decisions and balance competing football, commercial and operational demands.

Desirable Experience / Skills / Qualifications
  • Significant experience maintaining a stadium pitch within professional football.
  • NVQ Level 3 or above, or equivalent qualification, in Sports Turf Management.
  • PA1 / PA2 / PA6 or equivalent relevant pesticide qualifications.
  • IOSH or equivalent Health & Safety qualification.
  • Experience of hybrid pitch systems and associated specialist technology.
  • Experience managing major pitch renovation or reconstruction projects.
  • Experience managing playing surfaces used for both elite sport and non-football events.
  • Experience using turf performance monitoring and management information to inform maintenance programmes.

Personal Qualities
  • Exceptionally high standards and attention to detail.
  • Strong leadership and people-management capability.
  • Proactive and solutions focused.
  • Calm and decisive under pressure.
  • Reliable and accountable.
  • Commercially aware and able to balance pitch protection with the wider operational requirements of the Club.
  • Collaborative approach to working with football, commercial and operational departments.
  • Strong work ethic and personal credibility.
  • Flexible approach to working hours in line with fixtures, events and operational demands.

Additional Information 

Due to the nature of professional football and stadium operations, flexibility is required, including evenings, weekends and public holidays where operationally necessary.

Requirements

Grounds & Playing Surface Management

  • Lead all aspects of preparation, maintenance and presentation of the Craven Cottage playing surface.
  • Ensure the pitch is maintained consistently to elite professional football standards.
  • Develop, implement and monitor annual and seasonal turf management programmes.
  • Plan and undertake mowing, aeration, fertilisation, irrigation, overseeding, topdressing, plant health and disease management programmes.
  • Monitor pitch condition and performance through appropriate testing, inspection and record keeping.
  • Monitor weather forecasts and ground conditions and adapt maintenance programmes accordingly.
  • Manage playing surface usage to protect pitch quality, recovery and long-term performance.
  • Maintain the highest standards of pitch presentation, including line marking, goal preparation and matchday set-up.
  • Plan and deliver annual and in-season renovation programmes.

Football, Pitch Use & Events
  • Ensure the playing surface is fully prepared and presented for all First Team home fixtures.
  • Prepare and maintain the playing surface for approved Women’s and Academy fixtures and other football activity at Craven Cottage.
  • Work closely with Football Operations to understand fixture requirements and ensure appropriate preparation and recovery periods.
  • Work with Stadium Operations, Commercial and Events teams in planning pitch hires, events and other approved uses of the playing surface.
  • Assess proposed pitch activity and provide professional advice on its likely impact on surface condition, recovery and future football requirements.
  • Support the Club in maximising appropriate use of the stadium pitch while protecting playing quality and long-term surface performance.
  • Plan appropriate protection, preparation and reinstatement measures for non-football activity.
  • Assess weather and pitch conditions ahead of fixtures and events and advise relevant Club personnel on risks or required interventions.
  • Coordinate post-use recovery and maintenance activity to maximise surface recovery between fixtures and events.
  • Ensure goals, nets and other grounds-related football equipment are prepared, maintained and compliant with relevant requirements.
  • Liaise effectively with match officials, football authorities, visiting clubs, event organisers and other relevant parties on playing surface matters where required.

Pitch Infrastructure & Technology
  • Manage and monitor irrigation, drainage, undersoil heating and other pitch infrastructure.
  • Manage the effective deployment and maintenance of specialist turf equipment and technology.
  • Monitor the performance of pitch systems and identify maintenance, renewal or improvement requirements.
  • Ensure faults and performance issues are identified promptly and appropriate remedial action is taken.
  • Work with specialist contractors and consultants where required.

Team Leadership
  • Lead, manage and develop the Craven Cottage grounds team, comprising three direct reports.
  • Allocate duties, manage rotas and ensure appropriate staffing coverage across fixtures, events and operational requirements.
  • Set clear standards for performance, conduct and attendance.
  • Ensure team members are appropriately trained, qualified and competent for the work undertaken.
  • Conduct performance reviews and support continuing professional development.
  • Promote a positive, professional, accountable and collaborative team culture.
  • Ensure sufficient resilience exists within the team to maintain required standards during holidays, absence and periods of intensive stadium activity.

Equipment & Materials
  • Manage all grounds machinery, vehicles, tools and specialist equipment based at Craven Cottage.
  • Ensure equipment is appropriately stored, maintained, serviced and operated.
  • Maintain appropriate machinery replacement and lifecycle plans.
  • Manage the procurement, storage and control of fertilisers, pesticides, seed, materials and other grounds consumables.
  • Ensure appropriate stock levels are maintained while achieving value for money.
  • Ensure all chemicals and controlled materials are stored, used and disposed of safely and in accordance with applicable requirements.

Financial Management
  • Prepare, manage and monitor the Craven Cottage grounds operating budget.
  • Support annual CAPEX planning and prepare investment proposals for machinery, infrastructure and playing surface improvements.
  • Control departmental expenditure and ensure effective procurement and value for money.
  • Manage contractor expenditure and monitor performance against agreed scopes and budgets.
  • Provide appropriate financial and operational reporting.

Projects & Continuous Improvement
  • Lead closed-season pitch renovation and reconstruction works.
  • Develop proposals for pitch, machinery and infrastructure improvements.
  • Manage grounds-related projects from specification and procurement through to implementation.
  • Work effectively with specialist contractors, consultants and suppliers.
  • Maintain an up-to-date understanding of developments in sports turf management, agronomy, machinery and pitch technology.
  • Identify opportunities to improve playing surface quality, efficiency, sustainability and operational resilience.

Health, Safety & Compliance
  • Ensure safe systems of work are established and followed across all grounds operations.
  • Ensure appropriate risk assessments, method statements and operating procedures are in place.
  • Maintain a thorough working knowledge of relevant Health & Safety requirements associated with grounds operations.
  • Ensure the safe operation of machinery and vehicles and the safe use, storage and disposal of pesticides, fertilisers and other substances.
  • Ensure employees and contractors are appropriately trained, briefed and supervised.
  • Maintain appropriate departmental records relating to machinery, chemicals, maintenance, inspections and statutory requirements.
  • Respond appropriately to emergencies and report hazards, incidents or breaches promptly.

Communication & Collaboration

  • Maintain strong working relationships with Football Operations, Stadium Operations, Commercial, Events and other Club departments.
  • Communicate clearly regarding pitch condition, planned works, operational constraints and playing surface availability.
  • Provide clear professional advice on the suitability and timing of proposed pitch use, including football, commercial hires and events.
  • Work collaboratively with the Head of Grounds & Estates – Training Ground to share knowledge, resources and best practice where appropriate.
  • Maintain effective relationships with suppliers, contractors, consultants and football industry contacts.
  • Provide professional advice to the Chief Operating Officer and other senior management on playing surface matters, investment requirements and operational risks.

job.title: Chef De Partie
job.html_description:
Position Purpose 
 

  • We are looking for a chef with a background in catering for professional sports teams to join our passionate nutrition focused team.

  • You will support our Head Chef and Sous Chef in providing balanced, nutritional and high quality meals to our players and support staff at the training ground.

  • A good basis of nutrition helps our players to achieve their individual nutritional goals, ultimately enhancing health, recovery and performance.

  • To lead the kitchen team in preparing and providing meals to our youth and women teams.

  • Some travel with teams to away games may be necessary, following their weekly schedule/fixtures, ensuring all food provided to them meets the presentation, taste and performance need of the group.

Requirements

Requirements and Responsibilities
 

  • Work with the Head Chef and independently to create and develop exciting seasonal menus. 

  • Prepare meals for youth and women teams working within the nutritional guidelines and ensure junior team members are working correctly to achieve this with you.

  • Instruct junior team members accordingly to ensure youth and women teams' meals are delivered on time and presented to a high standard.

  • Support and lead junior members of the kitchen team.

  • Check stock requirements and order accordingly in the Head/Sous chef absence.

  • Travel with teams in the UK and abroad when required as the catering team representative and provide food provisions as requested.

  • Assist in the preparation of all travel food requirements whilst displaying good organisational skills.

  • Support Head/Sous chef to deliver constantly high quality food in a timely manner.

  • Cover Sous chefs' role as and when required.

  • Working closely with the Supervisor to ensure the highest level of food safety and hygiene are maintained. Compliance with COSHH.

  • Flexibility to work around the teams schedules.



Essential and Desirable
 

The Chef De Partie must have: 

  • Minimum of 1 year experience providing food to sports teams/athletes
  • Level 2 NVQ Professional Cookery or equivalent
  • Excellent communication skill to lead the junior kitchen team
  • Works well under pressure with the ability to remain calm with last minute schedule changes
 
Ideally, the Chef De Partie will: 
  • Football specific experience
  • Level 2 Food Hygiene certificate
  • Performance nutrition knowledge

job.title: Casual Academy Scout (Midlands)
job.html_description:
The National Academy scouting team is responsible for identifying and monitoring players either from grassroots or other Academies in national regions. They will complete reports on players and share information with other Academy staff to develop a range of player intelligence across the local area. 

There is a particular interest for us to recruit within the following teams: 
- Grassroots – Midlands 
- Academy- Midlands

Responsibilities

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:
• To manage your individual weekend schedule and regularly attend fixtures within your region or
across your phase.
• To complete reports on players all players with potential across your region and phase.
• Network with other national scouts to share information on potential target players.
• To keep National and department Managers informed of high potential players across their area or
age phase.
• To support with the ongoing communication to the families of players within our TID programmes
and on trial as and when required.
• To support the delivery of Talent ID programmes and events as and when required.
• Participate in scouting team meetings to further discuss succession planning and their identified
target players.
• To attend department meetings and participate in all CPD and required safeguarding training when
appropriate.

Requirements

The Casual Academy Scout (Midlands) must have:
• Knowledge and networks within the local area they scout.
• Previous experience scouting for another Academy (Cat 1, 2 or 3)
• FA Talent ID Level 2
• FA Safeguarding

Ideally, the Casual Academy Scout (Midlands) will:
• Previous experience scouting for another Cat 1 Academy.
• FA Level 2 Coaching
• Full Driver’s License

job.title: Academy Performance Scientist
job.html_description:
To deliver and support the physical performance provision across the Youth Development Programme (YDP), with a primary focus on the Foundation Phase (FP), working collaboratively with the multidisciplinary team (MDT) to support the club’s values and culture within the Fulham FC Academy Performance Department. The post holder will play an important role in supporting the physical development of academy players through age-appropriate, evidence-based sport science and strength and conditioning practice.
 
Alongside the primary delivery focus, the role will contribute to the Performance Department’s data strategy, supporting an evidence-based approach to the collection, analysis and visualisation of data to inform practice and decision-making across the department. The post holder will work collaboratively with Performance Department staff to improve the accessibility, interpretation and application of data within day-to-day practice and the ongoing evaluation of the academy performance programme.

Responsibilities

The Academy Performance Scientist must have: 
  • BSc Degree in Sports and Exercise Science or relevant subject.
  • MSc in related subject area.
  • BASES Accreditation.
  • Proficiency and experience in using Power Bi for data visualisation. 
  • Previous experience working with elite athletes, specially within the ages 9-16. 
  • Demonstratable experience working collaboratively in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary environment. 
  • Current EFAiF or the ability to obtain prior to start date.
  • Current FA Safeguarding Children Certification
 
Ideally, Academy Performance Scientist will: 
  • Knowledge of the Elite Player Performance Plan (EPPP) and the corresponding expectations associated with working at a Category 1 Academy.   

Requirements

This role will primarily support the delivery of the physical performance programme across the Youth Development Programme (YDP), with a particular focus on the Foundation Phase (FP). The post holder will work closely with the multidisciplinary team (MDT) to support the physical development of individual players through age-appropriate, evidence-based practice. Alongside applied delivery, the role will contribute to the Performance Department’s data strategy, supporting the effective collection, analysis and visualisation of data to inform player development, practitioner decision-making and ongoing evaluation of the programme.
 
The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role: 
  • Deliver high-quality physical performance support across designated FP and YDP age groups, across both pitch and gym-based environments.
  • Support the Lead Academy Performance Coach (U9-U16) with the design, delivery and ongoing evaluation of the FP physical development programme, ensuring provision is age and developmentally appropriate.
  • Collaborate with coaching, medical and wider MDT staff to develop and deliver individual physical development priorities aligned to players’ Individual Learning Plans (ILPs).
  • Contribute actively to MDT meetings and player review cycles, ensuring relevant physical performance information is appropriately interpreted and used to inform player development.
  • Lead the planning, delivery and reporting of physical performance testing within the FP and support testing provision across the wider YDP as required.
  • Support the collection, monitoring and interpretation of growth and maturation data, ensuring relevant information is effectively communicated and used to inform individual player programming and training decisions.
  • Collaborate with medical and performance staff to support the planning and delivery of late-stage rehabilitation and return-to-performance programmes within the YDP.
  • Support the physical preparation and development of players transitioning between age groups and phases, ensuring appropriate communication and continuity of individual programmes.
  • Contribute to the development and implementation of the Performance Department’s data strategy, supporting consistent and evidence-based approaches to data collection, analysis, reporting and visualisation.
  • Support the development of effective dashboards, reporting tools and data visualisations that make relevant performance information accessible and meaningful to practitioners and the wider MDT.
  • Work collaboratively with Performance Department staff to identify meaningful performance metrics and ensure data collection is purposeful, reliable and aligned to player and programme needs.
  • Analyse and interpret physical performance data to provide relevant insights that support individual player development, programme planning and practitioner decision-making.
  • Support the development of processes that improve the quality, consistency and efficiency of data collection and reporting across the Performance Department.
  • Contribute to the ongoing evaluation of the physical performance programme, using relevant data and evidence to identify trends, inform practice and support departmental learning and development.
  • Maintain effective communication and collaborative working relationships with Performance, Medical, Coaching and wider Academy staff to support an integrated approach to player development.
  • Contribute to Academy Performance Department targets, projects and improvement initiatives, supporting their monitoring and review where appropriate.
  • Support Academy events, including player and parent inductions, education sessions and workshops, where required.
  • Complete relevant administrative and operational duties associated with the role, ensuring records, reports and performance information are accurate and maintained appropriately.
  • Support and collaborate with all members of the Performance Department, consistently upholding the department’s philosophy, standards and culture.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality regarding all player information and club matters.
  • Demonstrate the highest standards of safeguarding practice, adhering to all relevant club policies, procedures and requirements.

Benefits

We expect to close applications on Friday 25th September, but if we receive a high level of interest, we may close the vacancy sooner. To avoid disappointment, please submit your application at the earliest opportunity.

Lead the planning, delivery and reporting of physical performance testing within the FP and support testing provision across the wider YDP as required. - Support the collection, monitoring and interpretation of growth and maturation data, ensuring relevant information is effectively communicated and used to inform individual player programming and training decisions. - Collaborate with medical and performance staff to support the planning and delivery of late-stage rehabilitation and return-to-performance programmes within the YDP. - Support the physical preparation and development of players transitioning between age groups and phases, ensuring appropriate communication and continuity of individual programmes. - Contribute to the development and implementation of the Performance Department’s data strategy, supporting consistent and evidence-based approaches to data collection, analysis, reporting and visualisation. - Support the development of effective dashboards, reporting tools and data visualisations that make relevant performance information accessible and meaningful to practitioners and the wider MDT. - Work collaboratively with Performance Department staff to identify meaningful performance metrics and ensure data collection is purposeful, reliable and aligned to player and programme needs. - Analyse and interpret physical performance data to provide relevant insights that support individual player development, programme planning and practitioner decision-making. - Support the development of processes that improve the quality, consistency and efficiency of data collection and reporting across the Performance Department. - Contribute to the ongoing evaluation of the physical performance programme, using relevant data and evidence to identify trends, inform practice and support departmental learning and development. - Maintain effective communication and collaborative working relationships with Performance, Medical, Coaching and wider Academy staff to support an integrated approach to player development. - Contribute to Academy Performance Department targets, projects and improvement initiatives, supporting their monitoring and review where appropriate. - Support Academy events, including player and parent inductions, education sessions and workshops, where required. - Complete relevant administrative and operational duties associated with the role, ensuring records, reports and performance information are accurate and maintained appropriately. - Support and collaborate with all members of the Performance Department, consistently upholding the department’s philosophy, standards and culture. - Maintain strict confidentiality regarding all player information and club matters. - Demonstrate the highest standards of safeguarding practice, adhering to all relevant club policies, procedures and requirements.
Benefits
We expect to close applications on Friday 25th September, but if we receive a high level of interest, we may close the vacancy sooner. To avoid disappointment, please submit your application at the earliest opportunity.

job.title: Ticketing and Membership Executive - Match Days
job.html_description:
In this role, you will work as a casual member of the team, as part of the wider Ticket Office team at Craven Cottage to manage inbound enquiries across a number of different communication channels – phone, email, online and in person – and deliver on the sale of commercial products relating to Fulham Football Club through the Club’s ticketing system, Ticketmaster.
   
The Ticket Office team form a critical part of the sales structure of the business, and you will be required to proactively support the Club in its objective to make it easy for people to buy from Fulham FC by assisting with supporter queries on our busy matchdays.  
  
You will form part of the team working as the first line of contact for our fans’ inquiries and as such we expect a high level of customer service and support at all times.  
 
You will be asked to provide assistance to the Head of Ticketing and the Deputy Supporter Centre Manager with a variety of Ticket Office duties as required. A good level of communication will be required.  

Hours of work 
This is a casual role, and there are no guaranteed hours. Working hours will vary according to business needs, match schedules and Club events. Successful candidates must be available to work evenings, weekends and all Fulham FC home league fixtures where required.

Responsibilities

The Ticketing and Membership Executive - Match Days must have: 
  • Customer Service experience
  • A good IT and technology systems understanding
  • Competent with all Microsoft Office Products
  • Ability to deal with the public with a focus on service excellence 
  • Able to work under pressure 
  • Ability to communicate with and relate to staff members at all levels 
  • Work on own initiative / creative 
  • Respect for confidentiality 
  • Flexible attitude to work tasks 
  • Genuine commitment to provide high quality customer service 
  • Positive ‘can do’ approach 
  • Desire to learn with enthusiasm

Ideally, The Ticketing and Membership Executive - Match Days will have: 
  • Previous experience with Ticketing Systems
  • Experience in a sales role

Requirements

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role: 
  • Providing service excellence when dealing with the Clubs customers (supporters, staff etc), at all times, serving customers in a polite, courteous and professional manner  
  • Handling any customer queries and complaints with a solution driven and positive approach  
  • Processing all ticket sales for Fulham FC products, away games and supporter travel, with daily reconciliation of all sales through the Ticketmaster system   
  • Updating and maintaining supporter database records to ensure data is accurately captured across the Ticketing System (Ticketmaster) and CRM System  
  • This role will be required to work all home league matchdays – on evenings or weekends , and an other ad-hoc fixtures or events as required   
  • You may also be required to carry out other tasks, not listed, to assist in the efficient operation of our business.  At all times you will be required to act in accordance with FFC company policies, follow departmental procedures and maintain the highest level of confidentiality.

job.title: Matchday Announcer (Fulham FC Women)
job.html_description:
Be the Voice of Fulham FC Women
Fulham Football Club is looking for a confident, energetic and charismatic Matchday Announcer to help create unforgettable experiences for our supporters throughout the Fulham FC Women season.

This is a unique opportunity to become the voice of Fulham FC Women, bringing energy, personality and professionalism to every matchday. From building excitement before kick-off to keeping fans engaged throughout the game, you'll play a central role in delivering an exceptional supporter experience.

Beyond matchdays, you'll also have opportunities to host selected club events and feature in on-camera presenting content, helping to raise the profile of Fulham FC Women across the Club's platforms.

If you thrive in front of a crowd, love live events and have a passion for connecting with people, we'd love to hear from you.

About the role
As Matchday Announcer, you will be responsible for engaging supporters before, during and after Fulham FC Women home fixtures at Motspur Park, as well as selected matches held at Craven Cottage.

Working closely with matchday operations, marketing and wider club teams, you'll help create a vibrant, family-friendly atmosphere that reflects the passion and ambition of Fulham FC Women.

Availability is required for all home fixtures throughout the season, including selected midweek matches.

Responsibilities

  • Acting as the official Matchday Announcer for all Fulham FC Women home fixtures.
  • Delivering pre-match, in-game, half-time and full-time announcements, including team news, goals, substitutions and key match information.
  • Communicating important safety information, sponsor messaging and club announcements.
  • Hosting supporter activations, competitions, games and quizzes to enhance the fan experience.
  • Conducting pitch-side interviews with supporters and guests where appropriate.
  • Supporting selected Fulham FC events as a host or presenter.
  • Creating and presenting on-camera content for Fulham FC Women and wider Club channels.
  • Contributing ideas that help develop and enhance the overall matchday entertainment experience.

Requirements

This is an exciting opportunity to be at the heart of one of the fastest-growing areas of the game. You'll play a key role in shaping the matchday experience for our supporters, helping to drive the continued growth and visibility of Fulham FC Women while representing one of football's most historic clubs.

Be the voice. Build the atmosphere. Help create memorable matchdays for Fulham FC Women.

Benefits

Essential
  • A confident and engaging presenter with excellent communication skills.
  • Comfortable interacting with crowds of different sizes, ages and backgrounds.
  • Able to adapt your style and energy to suit different audiences and moments.
  • Professional, reliable and organised, with the ability to deliver accurate and timely announcements.
  • A team player who enjoys collaborating with colleagues to deliver an exceptional supporter experience.
  • Available to work all Fulham FC Women home fixtures, including selected evening and midweek matches.
Desirable
  • Previous experience in a matchday announcer, presenter, host, MC or similar live event role.
  • Experience conducting live interviews and audience engagement activities.
  • A passion for football and understanding of the matchday environment.

Applications close Friday 18th September

job.title: Kitchen Porter
job.html_description:
To assist the Kitchen and Front of house staff in cleaning of all kitchen items, equipment,
machinery, floors and surfaces. Maintaining high standards and safe practices in all areas.
This is generally a Monday to Friday role however some flexibility with working hours will be
required on occasions and there is opportunity to gain basic kitchen skills.

Responsibilities

  • Manning the Pot Wash area
  • Cleaning numerous kitchen items used by the kitchen and also front of house
  • To maintain a very high standard of kitchen/food hygiene at all times
  • To maintain a high standard of personal hygiene at all times
  • The cleaning of the kitchen area including machinery, storerooms
  • Putting away incoming goods in storage areas and maintaining these areas

Requirements

Essential

  • 3 months in a similar role
  • Good command of the English language
  • Basic Food Hygiene
  • Able to work at a quick pace
  • Likes to get stuck in
  • Good team Player

job.title: Academy Kit Assistant
job.html_description:
The Academy Kit Assistant supports the smooth day-to-day running of the Academy by preparing, maintaining, and distributing training and match kit for players and staff. 

Responsibilities

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role:  
  • Prepare and distribute training and match kit. 
  • Ensure all kit and equipment is clean, organised, and ready for use. 
  • Assist with stock control, kit issuing, and inventory management. 
  • Support academy training sessions, fixtures, and tournaments as required. 
  • Maintain high standards within the kit room and storage areas. 
  • Work closely with academy staff to meet operational needs. 

Requirements

The ideal candidate will:
  • Be organised and reliable. 
  • Have strong attention to detail. 
  • Be a positive team player with a flexible approach to working evenings and weekends. 
  • Have a Full Driving License  
  • Be able to work in a fast-paced football environment while maintaining high professional standards.

job.title: Senior Groundsperson
job.html_description:
Work under the direction of line manager, to develop and maintain all of Fulham Football Clubs pitches and landscapes. In line with the highest pitch parameters and maintenance standards expected by the Head of Grounds, Squad Management and Directors of the Club.

  • Ensure that the Club pitches are maintained to the highest standards.
  • Ensure that all machines, tools, equipment, and club properties are maintained appropriately.
  • Ensure that the Management Team are kept informed of progress with routine work and are notified of major issues as soon as they are identified.
  • Keep line manager and staff informed of pitch works, job lists and communicate any issues to relevant parties.
  • Liaise with outside users/contractors (as required)
  • Ensure that all materials and resources are effectively and efficiently utilised to minimise waste.

Day to day operational duties will include but are not limited too physical activities and 
operating machinery including.

  • Mowing. (Hand and ride on machines)
  • White line marking to a high standard.
  • Driving tractors & utility vehicles.
  • Moving frost covers in the winter.
  • Chemical spraying. (If qualified)
  • Hedge trimming and collection.
  • Weed picking.
  • Heavy lifting. (Bags of product e.g., 25kg)
  • Use of strimmer’s, blowers, and edger’s.
  • Moving of goals and dugouts around the training ground.
  • Aeration of pitches and adjacent areas 
  • Irrigation operation and watering duties. 
  • Daily diary entries. 
  • Pitch testing and data collection. 
  • Supervision of team operations. 
  • Grow light movement and maintenance. 
  • Checking/replacement of nets in line with h&s requirements.
  • Coupling up of trailers and other equipment to the back of tractors

Matchday / Weekend work (ROTA)

  • Provide pitch allocation for teams using Motspur park.
  • Liaise with squad and academy management for matches and training.
  • General maintenance of the pitches and landscapes.


Requirements

Essential

Experience:
  • Full driving license.
  • NVQ level 2 in sports turf or equivalent.
  • Experience of the sports turf industry.
  • Spraying qualifications pa1, pa2, pa6.
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to communicate at all levels. 
  • Ability to provide written and/or verbal progress reports to management.
Personal Qualities:
  • Physically fit
  • Ability to work unsupervised.
  • Ability to think on your feet and use own initiative.
  • Flexible attitude to work tasks and hours.
  • Respect for confidentiality.
  • Genuine commitment to high quality standards
  • Team worker 
  • Can do attitude. 

Preferred

Experience:
  • NVQ level 3 in sports turf or equivalent. 
  • 2+ years as a Groundsman.
  • Football pitch maintenance to a high standard.
  • Ability to identify and resolve problems.
  • Take responsibility of tasks
Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
  • Basic irrigation knowledge.
  • Tractor coupling knowledge.
  • Setting of machinery. 
  • Understanding of health and safety.
  • I.T. competent. 
  • Understanding of synthetic turf maintenance.
Personal Qualities:
  • Hard working
  • Flexible in doing extra work.
  • Works to a high standard 
  • Enjoys working as part of a team.
  • Friendly 
  • Good problem solver

job.title: Part-Time Graphic Designer
job.plain_text_description:
Fulham FC Foundation is seeking a creative part-time Graphic Designer to support the communications of Fulham FC’s official charity. This role will work across a wide range of digital and print design projects, helping to bring the Foundation’s visual identity to life across all programmes and activities.
Working within established brand guidelines, you will contribute to digital campaigns and front‑end design projects, while also bringing your own creativity and ideas to each brief. Design direction will be provided, but the ability to work independently will be key to success in this role.
If you are passionate about design, looking for a new challenge, and feel you can add value to our team, please visit hhtp://careers.fulhamfc.com/
*This job description should not be regarded as exclusive or exhaustive. It is intended as an outline indication of areas of activity and responsibility and will be amended in the light of the changing needs of the organisation
.
Closing date for applications is Wednesday 5 August 2026.
Salary range: £20k-£22.5k
First stage interviews will take place across Thursday 13th & Friday 14th August 2026, and second stage interviews will take place on Thursday 20th August 2026. Please ensure you are available to interview on these dates prior to applying.
The post is subject to an enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service check.
Fulham Football Club Foundation is committed to increasing diversity and maintaining an inclusive workplace culture. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of ethnicity, race, gender, religious belief, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability.
Applicants must have the right to live and work in the United Kingdom and be able to provide appropriate documentation for the duration of their employment.
Responsibilities
Your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:
• Designing and building digital assets, including social media graphics, flyers, presentations, and newsletters
• Implementing design briefs in line with the Foundation’s brand guidelines
• Supporting and contributing to the development of the Foundation’s visual identity across multiple platforms and mediums
• Managing multiple design briefs from concept through to final delivery
• Working to tight deadlines while following efficient resourcing and scheduling processes
• Supporting social media scheduling and posting across Foundation channels
• Assisting with asset management and the printing of marketing collateral
Requirements
The successful candidate will:
• Be able to manage multiple briefs and work under pressure to tight deadlines
• Demonstrate a strong portfolio showcasing a range of print and digital design work for varied audiences
• Have advanced working knowledge of Adobe Creative Suite, including Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign, as well as PowerPoint
• Hold a design‑related degree, or demonstrate equivalent experience through a strong portfolio
• Ideally have experience working within sport, community, or charitable organisations
Personal attributes
We are looking for a team player who is:
• Open to feedback and able to collaborate effectively
• Highly organised with strong attention to detail
• Able to problem‑solve independently
• Capable of blending creative vision with strategic thinking
• Values in-person collaboration and team culture (the role is office based)

job.title: Groundsperson - Craven Cottage
job.html_description:
Work under the direction of line manager, to develop and maintain the Craven Cottage Football Pitch and surrounding landscapes. With the target to achieve the highest pitch parameters and maintenance standards expected by the Head of Grounds, Squad Management and Directors of the Club.
 
Responsibilities (below are example responsibilities but this is not intended as an exhaustive list)
 
  • Ensure that the Craven Cottage is maintained to the highest standard.
  • Follow all health and safety regulations.
  • Ensure that all machines, tools, equipment, and club properties are maintained appropriately.
  • Assist current team with daily procedures which are not limited to Mowing, line marking, aeration, fertilising, top dressing, seeding, pitch light movements.
  • As a Grounds Person you will, in the main, work alongside our experienced staff who will assist you with wide range of jobs associated with maintaining The Club’s grounds.
  • Assist on matchday preparations and post-match works on the pitch.
  • Assisting in end of season pitch renovations

Matchday / Weekend work
 
  • Prepare and repair pitch before and after games. 
  • General maintenance of the pitch, landscapes & equipment.
  • Watering and pitch light movements.
  • Upload pitch testing results to software platform and inform Head of Grounds of any damage, disease or areas of concern which may affect pitch standard.
  • Due to Premier league scheduling there will be potential early morning start times and late evening finishing times.

Requirements


Essential


Experience:

  • Minimum   4 years in the sports turf industry. 
  • Full UK Driving licence.
  • PA1, PA2 & PA6 spraying certificates
  • Level 2 Sports Turf Management or equivalent. 

Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:

  • Excellent communication skills   with the ability to communicate at all levels.  
  • Ability   to provide written and/or verbal progress reports to management. 
  • Machinery maintenance and setup of machinery.

Personal Qualities:

  • Physically fit
  • Ability to work unsupervised. 
  • Ability to think on your feet and use own initiative.
  • Flexible attitude to work tasks and hours.
  • Respect for confidentiality.
  • Genuine commitment to high quality   standards
  • Team worker 
  • Can do attitude. 

 
Desirable
 

Experience:

  • Football pitch maintenance.
  • Ability to identify and resolve problems.
  • Take responsibility of tasks.
  

Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:

  • Understanding of health and safety.
  • Tractor driving along with towing.
  • Safe use of pitch grow lighting units.

 

Personal Qualities:

  • Hard working
  • Works to a high standard 
  • Enjoys working as part of a team. 
  • Friendly 
  • Good problem solver
  • Keen eye for presentation

job.title: Casual Physiotherapist
job.html_description:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a motivated and organised Physiotherapist to join the Fulham FC Foundation team, working in a casual capacity to support our ‘Football & Education’ teams. The successful candidate will provide injury assessment, treatment and rehabilitation services through a weekly clinic and deliver pitch-side medical support on matchdays.

This role will have two key responsibilities that will support our ‘Football & Education Programme’ to maximise player performance, enhance recovery, reduce injury risk, and minimise the risk to players during a pitch side medical emergency.

The successful candidates first responsibility will be providing a weekly injury clinic to our participants to make sure they are receiving correct treatment and advice to minimise any potential injuries. As well as supporting the coaching team to make sure that any injuries caused due to training methods are minimised.

Although this role is casual, with the hours varying across the season, meaning that there is no set timetable. There are some key times when the injury clinic and fixtures will occur. Therefore, the ideal candidate will have good availability during the late morning/early afternoons of the working week. Please be aware that some away fixtures will take up the majority of the working day.
Salary: £25 p/h


Responsibilities

Responsibilities will include:
· Deliver a weekly two-hour physiotherapy clinic for injured players.
· Assess, diagnose and treat football-related injuries.
· Develop and monitor rehabilitation programmes.
· Provide injury prevention advice and education.
· Maintain accurate treatment and injury records.

The role's second responsibility will be to provide medical and emergency support during match days across both our male and female teams. This responsibility will include:

· Attend designated fixtures as required.
· Provide pitch-side assessment and injury management.
· Deliver first aid and emergency medical care where necessary.
· Ensure medical equipment and supplies are maintained.

Requirements

The successful candidate must have an excellent knowledge of rehabilitation and injury prevention, with extensive experience of delivering these within a sporting background. You will also be expected to have experience of providing medical support during match days, and of having excellent organisation and communication skills to support the wider coaching team.

The following qualifications, skills and experience are essential:
· FA Intermediate Trauma Medical Management in Football certificate or equivalent first aid qualification. – Could get away with PHCIS Level 2.
· BSc in Physiotherapy or Sport Rehabilitation
· Sports Trauma Management or Emergency Aid in Sport qualification.

job.title: Casual Football & Sports Coach
job.html_description:
Fulham FC Foundation are currently seeking to recruit an enthusiastic and committed person to take up the casual position of Football & Sports Coach.

Reporting directly to our Operations Officers the Football & Sports Coaches are responsible for delivering high-quality football & sports coaching to children, young people and adults. This role involves delivery across a wide-range of FFCF programmes, including Skills Club, Development Centres, Soccer Schools, Primary Education, Kicks, Health & Wellbeing and DisAbility. This is a casual role where flexibility is essential, as the role necessitates involvement in supporting the delivery of programme activities as and when required.  

The successful candidate will be somebody who has prior experience delivering football & sports coaching sessions to children & young people in grassroots & school settings, holds at least a FA Level 1/Introduction to Coaching Football qualification and is committed to the charitable purpose of Fulham FC Foundation. 

As this role is casual, there is no set timetable. Sessions may be offered on an adhoc or regular basis, depending on the needs of Fulham FC Foundation. It is the responsibility of the Football & Sports Coaches to maintain consistent and effective communication with our Operations Officers in ensure the continuation of work. 

Whilst there is no obligation for Fulham FC Foundation to provide, or for the Football & Sports Coaches to accept, work. Football & Sports Coaches who do not work for an extended period of time, will be deactivated. 

The successful candidates should be available to work across at least one of the below times, in order to receive work. 

Weekday Afternoons –3-5 pm;
Weekday Evenings - 5-9pm 
Weekends – Saturdays – 8am to 12noon. 
Work in other timings is available, however on a far reduced frequency. 
Salary Range: £12.95 p/h to £16.50 p/h

Next steps: 
There is no closing date for this role. Applications will be reviewed on a bi-weekly basis.

If successful, you will join a vibrant team who are passionate about achieving the organisation's vision of “an active, inclusive and thriving community”, and you’ll have the opportunity to build on your existing skills through a variety of training and development opportunities and experiences.

*This job description should not be regarded as exclusive or exhaustive. It is intended as an outline indication of areas of activity and responsibility and will be amended in the light of the changing needs of the organisation.


Responsibilities

  • To act as an Ambassador for Fulham FC Foundation (FFCF), representing the organisation professionally in line with its values. 
  • To plan and deliver high-quality football and sports coaching sessions to children, young people & adults in-line with FFCF standards.
  • To provide a safe, positive and inclusive learning environment at all times,
  • To adhere to FFCF’s safeguarding policies and procedures, ensuring the timely reporting of any safeguarding concerns or incidents within sessions. 
  • To engage, include, inspire and grow participation across FFCF activities.
  • To support the transition of participants between different FFCF programmes and activities.
  • To champion opportunities for individuals from underrepresented groups within FFCF activities. 
  • To identify and support progression pathways for talented young people. 
  • To support the development of FFCF programmes through positive collaboration with Operations Officers. 
  • To support the promotion of FFCF programmes across the local community. 
  • To assist in data collection and completion of monitoring & evaluation on an ongoing basis.
     
     
     
     
     

Requirements

Essential: 

Experience: 
•  Delivery of football coaching sessions in a grassroots environment
•  Delivery of sports coaching sessions to children & young people.
•  Delivery within a primary school.
•  Working in a customer-facing role.

Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
•  Introduction to Coaching Football qualification
•  In-date FA Emergency First Aid 
•  In-date FA Safeguarding Children certificate
•  Base knowledge of and willingness to learn & contribute towards FFCF strategic aims. 

Personal Qualities:
•  A positive role-model for children & young people.
•  Ability to travel independently across South-West London, including transport of equipment.
•  Well presented, with a professional manner.
•  Positive, energetic persona. Able to build rapport with participants.
•  Excellent time-keeping & punctuality.
•  Willingness to learn & develop personally & professionally.

Experience: 
•  Delivery of football & sports coaching sessions in a Club Community Organisation (CCO).
•  Delivery of Physical Education within a primary school. 
•  Delivery within a classroom environment.
•  Marketing & Promoting participation activities in the community.
•  Delivering an activity to children & young people with a Disability.
•  Delivery of football & sports coaching sessions to females.

Skills, Knowledge & Qualifications:
•  FA Level 2/UEFA C in Coaching Football qualification (or higher). 
•  Additional PE/HLTA qualification
•  Mentoring qualification
•  Non-football NGB sports qualifications.

job.title: Pre-Academy & Development Centre Coach
job.html_description:
To develop, support and coach all players who participate in a Fulham FC Academy Pre-Academy or Development Centre session.

 

To embody the Academy’s behavioural values whilst delivering fun, engaging and exciting session.

Responsibilities

The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role: 

 

  • To contribute to a high quality coaching environment through thoughtful and energetic delivery
  • To collaborate effectively with the relevant centre Head Coach or Coaches, Pre-Academy Recruitment Manager. 
  • When required, to effectively support the running and development of talent at various Academy Pre-Academy or Academy Development Centres at the request of your line manager. 
  • To collaborate effectively with the wider academy team, driving high standards, sharing best practice and establishing strong opportunities for participant transitions between programmes. 
  • To attending any mandatory meetings as directed by your line manager
  • To safeguard all personnel when the centre is running and correctly dismiss and welcome children upon arrival.

Requirements

The Pre-Academy & Development Centre Coach must have: 

 

  • Experience working in a sports participation-based environment 
  • Experience of managing projects coaching football to young people, specifically primary school aged children.
  • Experience working as an individual as well as part of a team. 
  • Experience working with Microsoft Office
  • Hold a UEFA C License/FA Level 2 Coaching in Football
  • FA First Aid Qualification
  • FA Safeguarding Children in Football Qualification
 
Ideally, the Pre-Academy & Development Centre Coach will: 
 
  • Have worked in a Pre-Academy or Academy Development Centre
  • Have worked in an Academy setting
  • Have completed FA Talent ID Level 1 in Introduction to Scouting 
  • Have experience working in Scouting & Talent Identification
  • Have knowledge of recruitment processes

Benefits

We expect to close applications on 25th September, but if we receive a high level of interest, we may close the vacancy sooner. To avoid disappointment, please submit your application at the earliest opportunity.

job.title: u18 Head Coach
job.html_description:
We are seeking an experienced and passionate coach to play a key role in delivering and enhancing our Academy Performance Plan. The successful candidate will be responsible for planning, delivering and reviewing high-quality coaching activities that support the individual development needs of Academy players. Working across the player pathway, they will help ensure smooth and effective transitions from the U16 age group into the Professional Development Phase and from the U18s into the U21 programme, maintaining consistency in player development. The role will also contribute to the ongoing development of the Academy Performance Plan and Technical Plan, helping to drive continuous improvement and maximise player potential.

Responsibilities

The U18 Head Coach must hold or have:
  • Experience of coaching adolescents in a Category 1 and/or Premier League Academy setting.
  • Experience of supporting parents/carers of adolescents within similar settings.
  • Experience of delivering individual player development programmes (ILPs/IDPs) within a multi-disciplinary environment.
  • Hold appropriate and up to date qualifications to conform to Professional Game Academy Audit Company (PGAAC) and Premier League Youth Development Rules (PLYDR) requirements.
  • UEFA A Licence (FA Level 4 qualification), and remain up to date with associated CPD requirements.
  • FA Advanced Youth Award (FA Level 4 qualification).
  • Valid FA Introduction to First Aid in Football certificate.
  • Valid FA Safeguarding Children certificate.
  • Broad awareness of the football industry’s governing policies and youth football protocols, in particular the Premier League’s Youth Development Rules.
  • Knowledge of regulations, research and expected practices in relation to working with adolescents, with particular reference to safeguarding, well-being, social development and safety.
  • Be player/person-centred (individualised) in approach to development.
  • Have high-level interpersonal skills, including being an effective and adaptable communicator.
  • Demonstrate resilience towards the everyday rigours of high-performance environments.
  • Be diligent, hard-working, detail-driven and intrinsically motivated by the Academy’s mission.
  • Hold a forward-thinking, positive and optimistic mindset.
  • Be willing to hold honest and supportive conversations with parents, guardians or carers of Academy players.
 
Ideally, the Under 18 Head Coach will hold or have:
  • A minimum of 2 years’ coaching experience within the Professional Development Phase (U16–U21) at a Category 1 Academy.
  • Experience of leading or supporting the development of less experienced coaching staff.
  • Experience within the England Youth International pathway or equivalent representative football.
  • The FA Talent Identification Level 1 qualification.
  • A related higher education degree in coaching, analysis or sports science (or similar qualification).
  • Confidence, in the use of video/performance analysis platforms (e.g. HUDL or similar) to support individual player development.
  • Awareness of First Team environments and the holistic demands placed on elite level athletes.
  • Continuously demonstrates openness & inclusiveness.
  • Action orientated; solution focused.
  • Show pro-activeness and an ability to work around or overcome obstacles that others may find challenging.
  • Understand the importance of being a confident custodian for an organisation with history and tradition.

Requirements

The Under 18 Head Coach (‘U18 HC') is employed to prepare, deliver and review coaching activities in line with the Academy’s Performance Plan.
 
There is a specific requirement for the U18 HC to support individuals as they move into and through the Professional Development Phase by delivering on the agreed commitments within each players Individual Learning Plan (ILP) and leading the process of continual review and refinement supporting the programme to be suitably responsive to each individual’s dynamic needs.
 
This essentially makes the U18 HC responsible for the following, non-exhaustive list:
Preparing
  • Lead the creation and ongoing development of both Individual Learning Plans and the Age Group Plan for the U18s.
  • Play an active role in the transition of players from the U16 age group into the PDP, working closely with U16 coaching staff to ensure continuity of style, expectations and individual development priorities.
  • Lead and sustain frequent, consistent and supportive communication with all players and their families to support transitions into Professional Football.
  • Lead the Multi-Disciplinary Team to create seasonal, weekly and daily, team and individual training plans.
  • Lead the preparations of meaningful content for individual player (and parent) reviews.
  • Support the preparation of content for team and individual Performance Education, Physical Development and Psychology delivery, ensuring integration where possible.
  • Align video to team and individual commitments, supporting team and individual player development over time.

Delivering
  • Lead the delivery of team training sessions in line with the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (Technical Plan) specifically integrating team and individual outcomes into practice.
  • Lead the delivery of individual training sessions (both inside and outside of team training sessions) in line with ILP commitments.
  • Lead teams and individuals through fixtures, both home and away, as part of the age group games programme, ensuring we are appropriately competitive.
  • Lead teams and individuals through tours, tournaments and competitions aligning the environment design and coaching behaviours to the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan.
  • Lead the delivery of performance education sessions in line with the expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (Technical Plan).
  • Support the delivery of the U16 and U21 programmes, as needed.
  • Attend first team games and youth international football events as required.
  • Oversee the implementation of the Academy Values and Behaviours towards staff and players.

Reviewing
  • Lead the effective review of team training sessions in line with ‘reflection’ expectations outlined within the Academy Performance Plan (Technical Plan).
  • Lead the effective review of individual training sessions and their impact on player-coach relationships and player performance over time.
  • Review all team and individual match performances in all games programme, tours and tournament fixtures.
  • Coordinate the ongoing ‘rolling’ review of each player’s ILP, ensuring the creation of clear action plans, involving colleagues from different disciplinary backgrounds, through weekly MDT meetings.
  • Lead all player and parent review meetings, ensuring player and parent feedback is recorded and agreed actions are shared and followed up.
  • Ensure each player’s Performance Clock is up to date and accurate.
  • Ensure all players are provided with regular access to their personal performance data, highlighting key metrics in line with the Academy Technical Plan.
  • Support the feedback process for all trialists.

Leadership & Collaboration
  • Be an active role model for all Academy coaches across the pathway and wider Club environment.
  • Offer guidance and support to less experienced coaching colleagues, taking a specific and regular interest in the upper part of the YDP.
  • Act as a key point of connection between the U16 age group and the PDP, and support alignment between the U18 and U21 programmes.
  • Consistently demonstrate, and hold others to, the highest levels of professionalism.
  • Support the delivery of coach development events across the year, as required.
  • Be part of the Academy Technical Group, shaping the Technical Strategy for the long term.
  • In collaboration with the Head of Talent ID & Recruitment, support the retention and recruitment of Academy players, including feedback for trialists and identification of players ready to progress from the U16 age group.
  • In collaboration with the Head of Performance, coordinate the effective review of the physical development programme and performance of the age group fitness coach.
  • In collaboration with the Head of Insights, coordinate the effective review of the performance education programme and performance of the age group analyst.

Benefits

We expect to close applications on Friday 2nd October, but if we receive a high level of interest, we may close the vacancy sooner. To avoid disappointment, please submit your application at the earliest opportunity.

job.title: Academy Education Post-16 Teacher (Maternity Cover)
job.html_description:
We are seeking a highly motivated and organised Teacher to join our team on a fixed-term basis covering maternity leave. This role is expected to last for approximately 7 months from October 2026.

The Post-16 Teacher will lead on the delivery of the Academy’s scholarship education programme, primarily teaching the BTEC Level 3 in Sporting Performance and Excellence, as well as the Sporting Excellence Professional (SEP) qualification. You will consistently deliver outstanding teaching and learning in your own practice and play a key role in driving high standards of teaching and learning across the department. You will be responsible for ensuring players make good progress towards their target grades in each qualification.
 
The successful candidate will play a key role within the pastoral team, supporting the holistic, off-pitch development of our players. Operating across phases, the role’s primary purpose is to add value to all aspects of our players’ educational programmes and to contribute towards maintaining the Academy’s Category 1 status.

Responsibilities

The Post-16 Teacher plays a central role in delivering and developing the Academy’s education programme, with a particular focus on the BTEC Level 3 in Sporting Performance and Excellence and the Sporting Excellence Professional (SEP) qualification. This role involves delivering consistently high-quality teaching and learning, tracking and supporting academic progress, and contributing to the holistic development of players through mentoring, pastoral support, and leadership of key initiatives. The successful candidate will also support wider departmental responsibilities, including destination tracking, school liaison, and compliance with EPPP and Premier League education standards, ensuring that the Academy continues to provide bespoke education pathways for its players.
 
The following is a non-exhaustive list of the responsibilities of the role: 
 
  • To help ensure the Academy Mission is achieved.
  • Deliver the BTEC Level 3 in Sporting Performance and Excellence and the Sporting Excellence Professional (SEP) qualification.
  • Plan and deliver high-quality, engaging lessons that drive outstanding teaching and learning, ensuring all learners make sustained progress.
  • Develop and maintain high-quality departmental resources, including schemes of work and assessment materials.
  • Monitor, track, and support the academic progress of all scholars, using data to inform timely interventions.
  • Create a positive, inclusive learning environment that promotes the highest standards of behaviour for learning amongst learners.
  • Take ownership of professional development and actively engage in relevant training and CPD opportunities.
  • Coordinate and conduct regular academic and pastoral progress reviews with players and their schools across phases.
  • Support the delivery of the Academy Life Plan, ensuring alignment with player development objectives.
  • To support the Youth Development Phase Compensatory Education Programme.
  • Attend relevant department, phase-specific, and league-led education meetings.
  • Support post-scholarship destination tracking and transitions.
  • Act as a liaison for school engagement, particularly with YDP players.
  • Coordinate or support YDP education projects and events.
  • Ensure compliance with EPPP, Premier League, and external quality assurance frameworks, including preparation for audits and visits.

Requirements

The Academy Education Post-16 Teacher must have: 
 
  • Educated to degree level.
  • PGCE with QTS or equivalent.
  • Experience of delivering a BTEC at KS5.
  • Experience of delivering KS3 and KS4 curriculum.
  • A commitment to plan and deliver high-quality, engaging lessons that drive outstanding teaching and learning, ensuring all learners make sustained progress.
  • Working knowledge of BTEC qualifications.
  • A commitment and experience of supporting young people holistically.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage effectively with players, parents, and colleagues.
 
Ideally Academy Education Post-16 Teacher will have: 
 
  • Experience working within an elite sporting or performance environment.
  • Knowledge of Academy football and the Elite Player Performance Plan (EPPP).
  • Experience of delivering an A-Level.
  • Experience delivering the Sporting Excellence Professional (SEP) apprenticeship.
  • PE based teaching experience. 
  • Experience in coordinating or leading education programmes.
  • Experience of working with external partners, including schools and awarding bodies.

Benefits

The closing date for applications is Friday 4th September.

job.title: Casual Football & Sports Coach - Goalkeeping
job.html_description:
To deliver high quality football coaching sessions to accomplished & aspiring grassroots players aged 6 to 16.

To deliver football & sports sessions across the wider Foundation to a range of children, young people and adults.

The successful candidate will have availability on one or more of the following days:
Mondays 7.30pm to 9pm 
Wednesdays - 7.30pm to 9pm
Fridays - 5pm to 9pm


Responsibilities

To act as an Ambassador for FFCF and maintain and develop relationships to ensure high quality experiences for young people, partner organisations, other staff and customers

To effectively plan and deliver high quality football sessions in-line with coaching syllabus, philosophy and values.

To effectively support the development of individual players through the creation of individual development plans throughout the season.

To identify and support the development of progression pathways for talented young people

To effectively plan and deliver extra-curricular and community activities across the wider Foundation.

To support the transition between school-based activities, wider Foundation activities and where appropriate, other community activities

Assist in data collection and completion of monitoring for reports on an ongoing basis, within the timescales required

To work closely with Football Development Officer's to understand programme standards and attendance targets and support the promotion of FFCF activities

To support the smooth function of the Operations Department in line with the Foundation values and targets and work across programmes, when required

Requirements

Essential:

Experience
Leading goalkeeper specific football sessions to age groups U7 to U16
Delivery of extracurricular and community activities to all age groups


Skills and Qualifications:
Minimum of FA Level 1 in Coaching Goalkeepers, National Goalkeeping Course or equivalent experience
FA First Aid - in date
FA Safeguarding - in date
Ability to drive, has access to a car or ability to travel independently. 

Personal Qualities
Committed and motivated by the purpose of the Foundation 
Demonstrates respect for colleagues, partners and customers and when possible operates above and beyond expectations
Well presented with a good manner
Excellent punctuality
Ability to prioritise work and consistently meet deadlines
Effective communicator

Preferable:
Experience
Delivery in a Club Community Organisation (CCO)
Delivery of activity to young people with a Disability. 
Delivery of CPD events to coaches.
Delivery of Physical Education lessons to primary age children

Skills and Qualifications
FA Level 2 in Coaching Goalkeepers or UEFA Goalkeeping B Diploma
Non-football NGB sports qualifications
Mentoring qualification
Talent Identification qualification
Understanding of Physical Education standards in schools (Ofsted guidance)

job.title: Employee belonging to a protected category
job.location: Viale della Liberazione, Milano, MI, 20124, IT
job.html_description:
Are you a dynamic, precise person interested in the world of sport, media & entertainment? Would you like to join an international club and work in a young and stimulating environment? FC Internazionale is constantly looking for professionals belonging to the Protected Categories (art 1 l.68/99) with whom to get in touch in order to evaluate together future collaboration possibilities for one of our departments, such as, for example:


  • Supply Chain and Procurement
  • Technology
  • E-commerce and Product Development
  • Marketing and CRM
  • Social Media & Digital
  • Ticketing & Contact Centre

In order to best align your interests and our needs, please specify function and area of potential interest when sending your application. Would you like to join our team? Then what are you waiting for, send us your CV! We look forward to getting to know you!


Those most in line may be evaluated for future needs to strengthen company structures.

job.title: Stadium Operations Crew
job.html_description:
Description

 Inter Miami CF is looking for Part-Time Operations Crew supporting the Facilities and Operations Department with event set-up, execution, teardown, changeovers and daily operational tasks. 


Essential Duties and Responsibilities: 

  • Participate in the execution of stadium and training facility events & games, including set-up and post-event breakdown. 
  • Assist with maintenance, upkeep, and organization around the facility. 
  • Maintain a safe work environment. 
  • Perform other related duties as assigned. 
  • Must be able to lift 50+lbs and walk for extended periods of time. 

Requirements

  • Past employment or internship experience in game operations or facility management preferred. 
  • Exceptional reliability, interpersonal, communication and organizational skills required. 
  • Possess strong attention to detail. 
  • Must be able to perform manual labor duties and tasks. 
  • Ability to work non-traditional hours, in non-traditional settings, within a team atmosphere. 

 

Other Details: 

  • Hours of work are based off our events schedule and may vary. 
  • Bilingual applicants not required, but preferred. 
  • All applicants must pass a pre-employment background check. 
  • Applicants must have permanent authorization to work in the U.S. at the time of application. Please note that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship now or in the future, so candidates must already possess work authorization that does not require employer sponsorship. 


  Compensation: 

  • Inter Miami CF offers a competitive compensation package, medical, dental, vision, disability insurance, life insurance and 401k retirement plan.

 Must have work authorization to work in the U.S. on a permanent and ongoing basis and must not require work visa sponsorship from Inter Miami CF now or in the future to retain authorization to work in the United States. 


All applicants must pass a pre-employment background check. 


Inter Miami CF is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law

job.title: Ticket Office Representative
job.html_description:
Description

Join our Ticketing Operations Team as a Ticket Office Representative at Nu Stadium and help fans access the excitement of match day.


What You'll Do: 

  • Provide exceptional customer service to all guests at Inter Miami CF home matches and other events at Miami Freedom Park. 
  • Professionally and accurately sell tickets for all IMCF matches and events. 
  • Assist guests with mobile ticketing challenges and other ticketing related matters.
  • Greet all guests in a polite, professional and a friendly manner.
  • Proactively anticipate all guests’ specific concerns regarding their purchase, directions, stadium information and schedule of all events.
  • Assist with the distribution of tickets for guests and other stadium visitors.
  • Reconcile all daily sales without any overage/shortage occurring.
  • Work with other staff members to ensure a quality match/event day experience.
  • Available to work all Inter Miami CF home matches and other stadium events.
  • All other related duties as required

Requirements

  • Highly proactive, goal-oriented, and motivated with a positive attitude.
  • Customer service experience preferred.
  • Bilingual - English and Spanish a plus.
  • Knowledge of Ticketmaster and Archtics is a plus.
  • Demonstrated understanding of new technology and mobile apps.
  • Must possess reliable transportation to and from work for all games.
  • Prior customer service experience is a plus.
  • Ability to stand for 3-4 hours per time, hours at a time in various degrees of outdoor weather conditions, including but not limited to, extreme heat or rain.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including but not limited to evenings, weekends and holidays.


All Applicants must pass a pre-employment background check. 


Inter Miami CF is an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. 


Must have work authorization to work in the U.S. on a permanent and ongoing basis and must not require work visa sponsorship from Inter Miami CF now or in the future to retain authorization to work in the United States.
