job.title: Goalkeeper Manager, Extended National Teams
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


Reporting directly to the Head of Goalkeeping, the Extended National Team Goalkeeper Manager will be responsible for educating, equipping, and developing our top talents through age-appropriate, skill-building approaches with the goal of grooming players to play for our Senior Extended National Teams. This role requires the implementation of coaching expertise, excellent in-person and remote communication skills, and collaboration with peers in identifying, selecting, developing, and transitioning talents through the player pathway and from other forms of the game.


Primary Responsibilities

  • Reports to the Head of Goalkeeping
  • Collaborates with the Director of Extended National Teams (Technical & Leadership), Beach, Futsal and Extended Head Coaches and Technical staff to create the best aligned environment for our players within US Soccer set structure and processes (THE U.S. WAY) Serves as the Goalkeeper Coach across Extended National Teams as needed
  •  Works to support and lead a high-performance environment for the Extended National Teams
  • Oversee the individual development and performance environment for goalkeepers 
  • Creates the conditions for an optimal on and off-the-field performance for players
  • Commits to delivering consistently to players the vision, mission, and objectives of U.S. Soccer and the overarching sporting strategy
  • Ability to align and deliver the USSF Player Development Philosophy – The U.S. WAY language (cultural anchors, performance anchors, game model, methodology, etc.)
  • Delivers the US Player pathway document outlining our areas of focus for all ages and stages of the program
  • Works collaboratively with the Talent ID department to identify, report, record, and select high potential players across the pathway
  • Contributes to the overall talent identification audit process providing outstanding player insights to support the player decision process of player selection
  • Responsible for the international development of elite Beach, Futsal and Extended players of our country
  • Ensures all national team goalkeepers within their care have an up to date and robust IDP
  • Delivers with excellence and in line with the “plan, perform, reflect, refine” model
  • Engages in the process of robust post-camp reviews with the Head of Extended National Teams (Technical & Leadership) and Head of Goalkeeping and adopts the personal development plan accordingly
  • Drives a culture of building outstanding players, staff, and club relationship
  •  Supports the US Soccer club engagement program with regular strategic club and player in-club visits
  • Upon request of the Head of Extended National Teams and Head of Goalkeeping, contribute to the US Soccer Coaching Education Programs

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • USSF “B” License or higher (or comparable UEFA B)
  • Coaching experience within elite youth development
  • Passion for working with and the developing young players 
  • Proven history of developing the individual player
  • Excellent organizational and leadership skills to manage and lead self and others
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication combined with a professional demeanor
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook) and Video Editing
  • Understands child development and maturation
  • A passion for and knowledge of talent identification
  • Possesses a growth mindset 
  • Has the ability to work as part of a wider coaching team influencing coaching within the US Soccer landscape
  • Able and willing to work non-traditional hours, including evenings and weekends, as needed
  • Willing to relocate once National Training Facility is established in Atlanta 

Desired Qualifications

  • USSF A License or equivalent
  • Bilingual (English and Spanish)
  • Coaching education experience
  • Thorough institutional knowledge of U.S. Soccer’s mission, goals, technical plan, policies, practices, and procedures   

    

U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Manager, Fan and Soccer Community Experiences
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description

  

As soccer becomes one of the fastest-growing sports in the United States, the Manager, Fan and Soccer Community Experiences owns how it feels to be a U.S. Soccer fan — whether this is at matches, special events or digitally. At U.S. Soccer, we work across a range of audiences across the whole soccer community including coaches, players and referees, families, members and clubs who we consider all to be fans


This is a strategic role with three connected mandates. First, it sets the creative and operational standard for national team matchday experience. Second, it builds the programming slate for U.S. Soccer’s tentpole and special event moments — including for big tournaments including World Cup, SheBelieves Cup, Gold Cup or at U.S. Soccer international matches and marquee cultural moments that sit alongside them. Third, and cutting across both, it merges the physical and the digital so that any experience is not a one-day footprint but a connected fan journey: discovered on social, deepened on-site, extended through content, and measured end to end.


This role is a builder of repeatable systems as much as a producer of individual events. It defines the experience framework, playbooks, and quality bar that a growing team, a national vendor base, and a multi-city event calendar can execute against consistently — turning passion for the national teams into durable, measurable fandom.


What Success Looks Like


In year one, this role establishes a defined U.S. Soccer fan and soccer community experience strategy and standard applied consistently across every match and tentpole event; delivers a programming calendar that is planned in advance rather than assembled match to match; and demonstrates, with data, that integrated physical-plus-digital experiences outperform standalone ones on reach, relevancy and revenue.


Key Responsibilities


Strategy, Vision & Experience Standards

  • Own and evolve U.S. Soccer’s fan and soccer community experience strategy across matchday, tentpole, and special event moments, with a focus on emotional resonance, lifelong fandom, and brand affinity.
  • Define the multi-year experiential roadmap and the annual programming calendar, aligning it to business goals and audience expectations.
  • Establish the U.S. Soccer fan and community experience standard — the creative principles, quality bar, and brand guardrails that govern every fan-facing footprint — and build the playbooks that make it repeatable at scale.
  • Serve as an internal and external thought leader on fan and soccer community experiences, representing the discipline with senior stakeholders, partners, host committees, and industry forums.

Matchday Experience

  • Lead the strategy, programming, and execution of all national team matchday experiences, including Block Party, Fan HQ, pre-match fan zones, in-stadium moments, gate giveaways, and thematic experience zones, and how to bring in the wider soccer community.
  • Design the full matchday experiences arc — from the night-before fan party and Block Party through arrival, in-bowl experience, and post-match extension — as a single, intentional journey rather than a set of separate experiences.
  • Champion theme nights and culturally led initiatives that reflect organizational values, celebrate the diversity of the American soccer fanbase, and deepen inclusion.
  • Partner with Partnership Marketing to shape and deliver thematic partner experiences, ensuring commercial integrations enhance rather than interrupt the fan experience and meet best-in-class on-site execution standards.
  • Set venue and host-city experience requirements in partnership with Events, Production, Ticketing, and Security, and hold vendors and internal teams to them.

Tentpole & Special Event Programming

  • Build and own the programming slate for U.S. Soccer’s tentpole moments across major tournaments — World Cup, SheBelieves Cup, Gold Cup, and other marquee competitions and milestone events.
  • Program these moments as content and culture, not just logistics: curate talent, music, food, art, community, creator, and legend-led components that give each event a distinct identity and a reason to attend.
  • Develop repeatable event formats and franchises — watch parties, fan fests, community celebrations, supporter takeovers — that can travel across markets and scale year over year.
  • Lead programming for milestone and special events including grassroots and community moments, tied to national team activity and Federation priorities.
  • Build multi-market and multi-year plans for major competitions, coordinating with host committees, venues, civic organizations, and local partners well ahead of event windows.

Integrated Physical + Digital Fan Experience

  • Own the connection between physical and digital experience: ensure every experience is designed from the outset with a content, social, and data capture plan, not amplified after the fact.
  • Partner with Social, Content, Digital Product, and Communications to build always-on and moment-driven programming that reaches fans who cannot attend in person and converts them into attendees over time.
  • Direct the design of on-site digital touchpoints — app-driven experiences, activations built for capture and sharing, second-screen and in-venue content moments, and registration or data-capture mechanics that feed the fan database.
  • Work with Growth, Lifecycle Marketing, Insiders and other Federation teams to define and deliver a personalized fan journey across live, digital, and community platforms, ensuring experiential moments are triggers within the broader lifecycle rather than isolated events.
  • Partner with Ticketing and Growth Marketing to connect experience programming to attendance, membership, and revenue outcomes.

Partnerships, Supporters & Community

  • Cultivate relationships with supporter groups, vendors, civic organizations, and cultural partners to co-create experiences rooted in authenticity and local relevance.
  • Lead cross-departmental coordination with Events, Production, Ticketing, Consumer Products, Community Relations, Media Partnerships, Communications, and Brand to ensure alignment, consistency, and excellence in execution.
  • Manage agency and vendor relationships end to end, including scoping, selection, briefing, and performance management.

Insights, Measurement & Optimization

  • Establish the KPI framework for fan experience — spanning attendance, sentiment, dwell time, digital reach and engagement, data capture, and downstream ticketing and membership impact — and report against it to senior stakeholders.
  • Partner with the Insights team to analyze fan sentiment, survey feedback, and social performance, and translate findings into concrete changes to programming and design.
  • Run a disciplined test-and-learn approach, piloting new formats and retiring those that do not perform.

Team Leadership, Budget & Operational Excellence

  • Manage, coach, and develop the Fan Engagement Coordinator, setting clear priorities and creating room for that role to own workstreams independently.
  • Build and lead extended matchday and event teams, including seasonal staff, agency partners, and cross-functional working groups.
  • Own the fan experience budget end to end — planning, allocation, tracking, and reconciliation — ensuring resources are directed to the highest-impact moments and delivered on time and on budget.
  • Stay at the forefront of industry innovation in fan experience, live entertainment, and experiential technology, bringing forward ideas that keep U.S. Soccer at the leading edge.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Sports Management, Business, or a related field.
  • 6–8+ years of progressive experience in fan experience, experiential marketing, live events, or brand experience within sports, entertainment, or consumer-facing industries.
  • Direct people management experience, including coaching and developing junior staff.
  • Proven experience designing and delivering high-impact experiential programs at national scale, including large-scale or multi-market events.
  • Demonstrated fluency across physical and digital experience — able to brief a content and social team as credibly as a production vendor, and to design experiences for both on-site impact and digital reach.
  • Experience programming events as content: curating talent, cultural partners, and creative components, not only managing logistics.
  • Track record of owning and managing significant event budgets.
  • Comfort using data and fan insight to set strategy, prioritize investment, and evaluate performance.
  • Exceptional cross-functional collaboration, communication, and executive presence.
  • Ability to lead multiple complex initiatives simultaneously in a high-performance, fast-paced environment.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook)Flexibility to work non-traditional hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. 
  • Ability to travel approximately 40–50% annually, concentrated in match windows and tentpole event periods.


Desired Qualifications

  • Experience in international soccer, major league sports, music or live entertainment, or global event production.
  • Experience delivering fan experience programs for a large-scale event or major tournament.
  • Expertise in data-driven marketing, loyalty strategy, or direct-to-consumer fan experience design.
  • Bilingual or multicultural fluency to engage diverse audiences.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description

  

U.S. Soccer is seeking a collaborative and growth-oriented Senior Performance Coach to support the Women’s Youth National Teams. As a member of the Integrated Performance Support (IPS) department, this role will contribute to the delivery and continuous evolution of integrated performance practices through a female lens across camps, competitions, and other player development environments. 


Emphasizing that the female lens is at the heart of everything we do, this role aligns with the WNT strategy while integrating an interdisciplinary approach. This position will collaborate closely with Performance Medicine, Performance Nutrition, Performance & Data Analytics, Performance Innovation, and Technical staff to optimize player availability, development, and performance.


The Senior Performance Coach will support the design and implementation of evidence-informed physical preparation strategies, including readiness and load monitoring, physical testing, strength and conditioning, recovery, and performance planning through a female lens. In partnership with coaches and IPS colleagues, this role will help create world-class player experiences that support both team success and long-term player development.


A key focus of this position will be advancing U.S. Soccer’s commitment to becoming world-leading in female health, development, and performance. Working within the Arthur M. Blank National Training Center, the Senior Performance Coach will contribute to the development of integrated systems, innovative practices, and environments that elevate player care across the Women’s Youth National Team pathway.


The ideal candidate is an intellectually curious practitioner and strong teammate who thrives in collaborative, fast-paced environments, embraces innovation, and is passionate about supporting the growth of elite female players.


Primary Responsibilities


Integrated Performance Delivery

  • Support the delivery of integrated performance services across the U19-U20 Women’s National Team environments, including domestic and international camps and competitions.
  • Contribute to the design and implementation of individual and team-based performance strategies that optimize player availability, development, and performance.
  • Collaborate closely with technical staff on training design, competition preparation, recovery, and long-term player development.
  • Collaborate with WNT, U23 and other WYNT technical, performance, and medical staff to align club, college, and country communications, facilitate the exchange of information, and promote continuity of player care, to ensure smooth player transitions between club and country environments.
  • Travel with Youth National Teams to provide on-site performance support.

Female Health & Performance

  • Advance U.S. Soccer’s commitment to becoming world-leading in female health, development, and performance.
  • Support initiatives related to growth and maturation, female health, injury-risk reduction, and long-term player development.
  • Collaborate with performance medicine, performance nutrition, and technical staff to optimize player readiness and availability.

Physical Preparation & Performance Science

  • Support the design and implementation of physical preparation programs (using Teamworks AMS), including strength and conditioning, recovery, and load management strategies.
  • Oversee player monitoring, physical testing, and performance profiling systems to support evidence-informed decision-making.
  • Utilize technologies including PlayerData GPS, VALD performance tools, OURA, FitrWoman, Raw Stadia, and a growing portfolio of technologies to support health and performance.
  • Translate objective performance data into actionable insights for players, coaches, and IPS staff.
  • Contribute to the ongoing development of best practices in performance science across the women’s pathway.

Integrated Performance Support Collaboration

  • Serve as a key member of the Integrated Performance Support (IPS) team, supporting world-class player care and performance services.
  • Collaborate with Performance Medicine, Performance Nutrition, Performance & Data Analytics, Performance Innovation, and technical staff to support integrated decision-making and player development.
  • Execute and continuously improve performance methodologies, testing protocols, and operational standards across camps and competitions.
  • Contribute to a culture of curiosity, collaboration, accountability, and continuous learning.
  • Support the onboarding and development of network practitioners and interns as needed.

Data, Analytics & Innovation

  • Oversee the collection, interpretation, communication, and storage of player performance data in accordance with U.S. Soccer standards.
  • Partner with analytics and innovation teams to develop and implement novel approaches to player monitoring and decision-making.
  • Support longitudinal player profiling and talent development initiatives across the Women’s pathway.
  • Build and maintain relationships with clubs, universities, and external partners to facilitate the exchange of performance information and best practices.
  • Contribute to the National Training Center as a world-class environment for integrated athlete support, innovation, and organizational learning.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Master’s degree or higher in Sport Science, Exercise Physiology, Kinesiology, Strength & Conditioning, or related field.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting elite female athletes and/or female teams.
  • Certified Strength & Conditioning Specialist (CSCS), Certified Performance & Sport Scientist (CPSS), or equivalent international certification.
  • Minimum of 3–5 years of experience working in elite sport environments, including professional clubs, collegiate athletics, academies, or national teams.
  • Strong understanding of soccer and the physical demands of the international game.
  • Experience working within multidisciplinary and integrated performance environments.
  • Significant experience with athlete monitoring and performance technologies, including GPS, force plates, athlete management systems, and wellness platforms.
  • Ability to synthesize objective data and translate insights into practical recommendations for players, coaches, and staff.
  • Strong communication, planning, and organizational skills.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook).
  • Ability to work non-traditional hours, including evenings, weekends, and extensive domestic and international travel.
  • Current First Aid and CPR certification.

Desired Qualifications

  • Knowledge of female athlete health, growth and maturation, and long-term athlete development principles.
  • PhD in Sport Science, Exercise Physiology, Kinesiology, or related fields.
  • Experience supporting Youth National Teams, professional clubs, or elite female development pathways.
  • Experience working collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams.
  • Bilingual (English and Spanish).


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Maintenance Technician
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Maintenance Technician is responsible for the day-to-day operation, maintenance, and reliability of the National Training Center’s building systems. This hands-on role serves as the technical lead for all core infrastructure, including HVAC, electrical, plumbing, life safety, and building automation systems. Working within a small facilities team, the maintenance technician responds to work requests and performs maintenance and repairs throughout the facility.  


Primary Responsibilities

  

Building Systems & Technical Operations

  • Perform hands-on operation, inspection, maintenance, and repair of HVAC, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, lighting, and building automation systems.
  • Monitor system performance to ensure reliability, efficiency, and occupant comfort.
  • Respond to and resolve system issues, alarms, and failures in a timely and professional manner.

Preventive Maintenance & Reliability

  • Track equipment warranties and service agreements, ensuring required maintenance is conducted in accordance with warranty terms.
  • Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, inspections, and repairs.
  • Identify recurring issues and recommend corrective actions or capital improvements.
  • Support asset lifecycle planning by tracking equipment condition, warranty status, and replacement timelines.

Compliance, Safety & Documentation

  • Support compliance with applicable codes, regulations, and inspection requirements.
  • Perform and document routine testing of critical systems.
  • Maintain system documentation, manuals, drawings, warranties, and service records.
  • Assist with audits, inspections, warranty claims, and corrective actions.

Vendor & Contractor Oversight

  • Coordinate and collaborate with vendors and contractors.
  • Ensure work is completed safely, on schedule, and in accordance with scope and warranty requirements.

Event & Operations Support

  • Support facility readiness for events, training camps, meetings, and activations.
  • Provide on-site technical support during events.
  • Coordinate with Hospitality, Security, IT, and other departments.

Other Duties

  • Support special projects, system upgrades, warranty transitions, and operational initiatives.
  • Assist the Facility Engineer with standards and workflows. 
  • Other duties as assigned. 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in building engineering or facilities maintenance.
  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Strong hands-on experience with HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical systems.
  • Strong documentation and communication skills. 
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends (Saturday and Sunday), and holidays is required.
  • Ability to perform general manual labor and lift 50 lbs.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience in sports facilities or large campuses.
  • Technical certifications related to HVAC, plumbing, or electrical equipment.
  • Familiarity with CMMS and building automation systems.
  • Multilingual skills (Spanish preferred).
  • Passion for soccer.


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Director, Donor Experiences & Hospitality
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description

   

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Strategic Philanthropy, the Director, Donor Experiences & Hospitality will lead the strategy, development, and execution of U.S. Soccer's donor experiences and hospitality program, building on the successful donor engagement platform established during FIFA World Cup 2026 and positioning the Federation for the road to the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup and beyond. 


This leader will transform donor experiences and hospitality into a strategic fundraising platform that generates philanthropic revenue, cultivates, retains, and deepens relationships with U.S. Soccer supporters, and advances U.S. Soccer’s $250 million comprehensive campaign through meaningful, world-class engagement. 


Working collaboratively across Advancement and the broader Federation, the Director will establish the long-term vision, operating model, and standards for donor experiences while leading a team responsible for hospitality, fundraising events, and VIP engagement. Leveraging marquee matches, international competitions, the Arthur M. Blank U.S. Soccer National Training Center, and other signature Federation assets, this role will create scalable donor experiences that strengthen fundraising, stewardship, and long-term philanthropic growth. 


Primary Responsibilities 

  • Develop and lead a comprehensive donor experiences and hospitality strategy aligned with U.S. Soccer's fundraising priorities, the Federation's $250 million comprehensive campaign, and long-term philanthropic growth. 
  • Build and lead the donor experiences and hospitality function by establishing its operating model, strategic roadmap, hospitality standards, organizational structure, and scalable systems that support long-term fundraising growth. 
  • Hire, supervise, mentor, and develop a team of 2–3 direct reports, while assessing future staffing and organizational needs as the donor experiences function expands. 
  • Develop and execute an annual donor experiences strategy and calendar that intentionally supports cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, donor retention, upgrades, recognition, campaign priorities, and executive engagement. 
  • Design and oversee U.S. Soccer's portfolio of donor experiences, including cultivation events, fundraising events, stewardship and recognition activities, matchday hospitality, VIP experiences, campaign celebrations, behind-the-scenes access, and other engagement opportunities that strengthen philanthropic relationships and inspire deeper investment. 
  • Develop innovative donor experience strategies that directly support fundraising, including bespoke cultivation events, campaign experiences, premium hospitality opportunities, and future revenue-generating donor packages surrounding FIFA World Cups, international competitions, and other signature Federation events. 
  • Position the Arthur M. Blank U.S. Soccer National Training Center as a premier destination for donor engagement, stewardship, fundraising, and hospitality by creating innovative donor experiences that leverage one of the Federation's most distinctive philanthropic assets. 
  • Partner closely with Annual Fund, Stewardship, Major Gifts, Principal Gifts, Advancement Marketing & Communications, and Advancement Services to ensure donor experiences are intentionally designed to support acquisition, cultivation, stewardship, retention, upgrades, and fundraising outcomes—not simply event execution. 
  • Collaborate across Commercial, Sporting, Marketing & Communications, Event Operations, and other cross-federation departments to deliver integrated donor experiences aligned with Federation priorities. 
  • Establish standards, project management systems, operational procedures, and hospitality best practices that ensure donor experiences are executed consistently, efficiently, and at the highest level of quality. 
  • Develop and manage departmental budgets, hospitality investments, vendor relationships, venue contracts, and strategic partnerships while ensuring responsible financial stewardship. 
  • Establish key performance indicators and evaluation metrics to measure donor engagement, fundraising impact, donor retention, hospitality effectiveness, operational excellence, and return on investment. 
  • Identify emerging trends, innovative hospitality concepts, and best practices that position U.S. Soccer as a leader in donor engagement and philanthropic hospitality. 
  • Promote a culture of exceptional hospitality and donor-centered service throughout the Federation. 
  • Support the overall goals of the Advancement department. 
  • Perform other duties as assigned. 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required 
  • 8+ years of progressive leadership experience in advancement, fundraising, donor engagement, or donor experiences and hospitality, including experience building or significantly scaling experiential fundraising programs. 
  • Proven track record of generating philanthropic revenue through events and experiences 
  • Experience building from the ground up or significantly scaling donor experiences and hospitality programming 
  • Ability to build the strategy, systems, processes, staffing model, and measures of success for a growing function 
  • Experience hiring, supervising, coaching, and developing professional staff. 
  • Proven ability to think strategically while successfully leading complex initiatives from concept through execution. 
  • Strong project management, organizational, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Experience managing budgets, negotiating contracts, and overseeing vendor and partner relationships. 
  • Exceptional communication, collaboration, and relationship-building skills with the ability to influence stakeholders across all levels of an organization. 
  • Experience utilizing Salesforce or a comparable CRM platform preferred. 
  • General knowledge of soccer preferred. 
  • Must be able to connect "microt" details to "macro" vision and mission.
  • Ability to work evenings, weekends, and travel as needed. 
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook). 


U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Senior Project Manager, Creative Studio
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description

   

U.S. Soccer is seeking a highly organized, collaborative, and creatively minded Senior Project Manager to join our Creative Studio.

This role is a critical operational partner, helping establish the systems, processes, and workflows that enable the team to do its best creative work. The role will manage projects from intake through delivery, connecting creative teams with Brand Marketing, Content, Social, Partnerships, Events, Communications, and other stakeholders to ensure priorities, timelines, resources, and expectations remain clear.


The ideal candidate is an experienced creative project manager and producer who understands how creative work gets made. They can translate a brief into a clear plan, build realistic timelines and workstreams, identify dependencies and risks, coordinate internal and external resources, manage approvals, and keep complex projects moving in a fast-paced environment.

 

While the role leans heavily into creative operations and project management, a strong understanding of creative production is essential. This person should be comfortable jumping into production details when needed: from managing vendors and production partners to supporting photo/video shoots, creating production schedules, coordinating logistics, and ensuring final deliverables meet the creative and brand standard. This is a hands-on role for someone who brings structure and keeps creative work flowing.


Primary Responsibilities


Creative operations and managing projects

  • Own the day-to-day project management of Creative Studio work from intake through final delivery.
  • Manage the Creative Studio intake process, gathering requirements, clarifying objectives, confirming deliverables, and ensuring briefs are actionable and production-ready.
  • Translate creative briefs into clear project plans, timelines, workstreams, milestones, owners, and deliverables.
  • Develop and maintain workback schedules and project trackers across multiple concurrent projects.
  • Establish clear priorities, dependencies, decision points, and approval processes.
  • Monitor project health, proactively identify risks or blockers, and develop practical solutions to keep work moving.
  • Lead project status meetings, communicate next steps, document decisions, and maintain accountability across teams.
  • Help balance competing priorities and resources across the Creative Studio.
  • Protect creative teams from unnecessary operational drag while ensuring stakeholders have visibility into progress.
  • Identify opportunities to improve Creative Studio processes, workflows, tools, and ways of working.
  • Help build scalable creative operations practices that support the growth of the U.S. Soccer Creative Studio.

Functional Partnership

  • Serve as a central point of coordination between Creative and Brand Marketing, Content, Social, Partnerships, Events, Communications, and other Federation teams.
  • Partner with creative leads to understand scope, creative needs, resourcing, and production requirements.
  • Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders and external partners, bringing clarity to complex projects and competing needs.
  • Manage feedback and approvals, ensuring the right stakeholders are engaged at the right moments.
  • Clearly communicate project status, decisions needed, risks, and changes in scope or timing.
  • Help translate creative strategy and direction into executable plans without compromising creative ambition.

Creative Production

  • Support production of integrated brand campaigns, content, events, and other high-priority Federation moments.
  • Lead production planning when projects require photo, video, experiential, or other external production support.
  • Develop production schedules, call sheets, shot lists, crew briefs, itineraries, production books, and other materials as needed.
  • Coordinate production logistics including locations, vendors, talent/player needs, usage considerations, post-production schedules, and delivery specifications.
  • Manage digital, social, video, design, and campaign deliverables, including cutdowns, versioning, localization, and partner adaptations.
  • Coordinate with creative teams and production partners to ensure work is delivered to the expected creative and brand standards.
  • Step into hands-on production management when project needs require it.

Tools and Workflow Leadership

  • Own and maintain accurate project information, timelines, trackers, documentation, and workflow records.
  • Maintain strong working fluency in Airtable and Microsoft Office.
  • Help establish and maintain Creative Studio PMO processes and standards.
  • Look for opportunities to streamline repetitive processes, improve visibility, and create efficiencies across the team.
  • Ensure project documentation and status information are clear, current, and accessible to the appropriate stakeholders.

Vendor, Budget, and Logistics Management

  • Source, onboard, and manage external vendors, freelancers, and production partners as needed.
  • Coordinate photographers, videographers, production crews, stylists, fabricators, and other creative resources.
  • Support project scoping, estimates, SOWs, POs, budgets, and invoice tracking in partnership with internal teams.
  • Help determine the appropriate internal and external resources needed to deliver projects successfully.
  • Track project budgets and flag potential scope or cost issues early.

Quality and Consistency

  • Ensure projects are delivered on time, on budget, and at the quality bar expected for a national brand.
  • Maintain a strong understanding of U.S. Soccer's brand identity and creative standards.
  • Protect creative integrity while balancing timelines, budgets, resources, and operational realities.
  • Ensure final deliverables are accurate, complete, properly reviewed, and ready for launch or distribution.

Worktypes the Senior Project Manager will be involved in (Examples)

  • Campaign creative and rollout assets.
  • Event creative and experiential support materials.
  • Digital, social, and video deliverables including cutdowns, versioning, and localization as needed.
  • Partner-aligned creative adaptations.
  • Brand marketing collateral and design system extensions.

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • 5–7+ years of experience in creative project management, creative operations, production, or a related discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, integrated creative work across brand, digital, social, video, content, and design.
  • Strong project management fundamentals including scoping, scheduling, resourcing, budgeting, risk management, and stakeholder alignment.
  • Experience managing multiple projects and priorities simultaneously in a fast-paced creative environment.
  • Advanced proficiency in Airtable or comparable project/workflow management platforms.
  • Experience managing external vendors, freelancers, agencies, or production partners.
  • Strong understanding of creative development and production processes.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to lead meetings, document decisions, manage feedback, and drive approvals.
  • Ability to anticipate problems, identify dependencies, and proactively develop solutions.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook) and Google Workspace.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience supporting sports marketing.
  • Basic knowledge of soccer and U.S. Soccer
  • Familiarity with brand identity systems and maintaining consistency across diverse executions.
  • Working knowledge of usage rights and licensing considerations where relevant.

Key Attributes

  • Highly collaborative: Builds trust quickly across Creative and cross-functional partners and brings stakeholders into clarity rather than conflict.
  • Positive, steady presence: Maintains calm momentum under pressure and raises the team’s confidence during tight timelines.
  • Team-first operator: Prioritizes shared outcomes, makes teammates’ work easier, and steps in where needed without ego.
  • Culture-builder: Contributes to an environment of respect, accountability, and good communication including during high-volume periods.
  • High ownership, low drama: Flags issues early, proposes solutions, and keeps work moving without blame or noise.
  • Detail disciplined, creatively minded: Holds a high quality bar while understanding what it takes to ship work in the real world.


Success in This Role Looks Like

  • Projects stay on track because priorities, timelines, owners, and decisions are consistently clear.
  • Creative team capacity feels well-managed and stakeholders remain informed and aligned.
  • Risks are surfaced early with credible options, not surprises near launch.
  • Campaign and event executions deliver smoothly with strong craft and minimal last-minute rework.



U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

job.title: Senior Manager, Corporate Communications
job.html_description:
Description


U.S. Soccer Overview


The U.S. Soccer Federation exists in service to soccer. Our aim is to ignite a national passion for the game. Because we believe that soccer is more than a sport; it is a force for good.


We understand the importance and the power of teamwork, on and off the pitch. That is why we work closely with our Federation partners and members, to inspire, support and guide every level of the game: from the grassroots to the National Teams. We want to bring soccer into every home and every community, right across America. Because we believe that soccer can transform lives like no other sport. Soccer can represent the best of U.S.


U.S. Soccer is in a period of significant growth, with ambitious plans for U.S. Soccer in the near and far future. We are, therefore, looking for dynamic servant leaders to join us on this journey: in service to soccer. Applicants must be able to demonstrate visionary leadership, analytical decision-making, professional flexibility, and an empathic management style that builds bold teams and delivers globally significant results.


Position Description


The Senior Manager, Corporate Communications supports and executes enterprise-wide communications strategies that build understanding, strengthen relationships, create meaningful opportunities for engagement and ensure U.S. Soccer’s Federation membership base feels informed, heard and connected to the organization’s mission and direction. In close partnership with the Senior Director of Corporate Communications and business partners across the Soccer Growth and Member Strategy teams, this role is responsible for developing and executing both internal and external communications plans and initiatives that reflect U.S. Soccer’s strategic priorities and mission. 


The ideal candidate is a strategic, proactive and relationship-driven communicator with experience navigating complex stakeholder environments and aligning messaging that helps members and key stakeholders including referees, coaches and youth leaders understand how the organizations work affects them. Areas of focus include executive communications, member engagement, and cross-functional coordination. 


This role oversees the development of executive briefing materials, talking points, background documents, and presentations for public appearances, media engagements, and internal leadership communications as it relates to Soccer Growth and Member Strategy initiatives. This role also supports larger Federation external functions, including board meetings, annual member meetings, annual general meetings of member organizations, regional meetings and public-facing appearances. 


Success in this role requires strong cross-functional collaboration, the ability to synthesize complex information for diverse audiences, and a commitment to ensuring that U.S. Soccer’s internal communications infrastructure and external messaging are aligned and mission-driven. 


Primary Responsibilities 

  • Develop and execute corporate communications strategies that support organizational priorities and strengthen reputation among members, partners, media and other stakeholders. 
  • Develop executive communications, talking points, presentations, messages and other materials for internal and external audiences. 
  • Identify opportunities to proactively tell the organization’s story and demonstrate its impact. 
  • Build strong relationships across departments and serve as a communications thought partner to teams working directly with members and stakeholders. 
  • Collaborate with marketing, digital, events, executive leadership, advancement and other teams to create integrated engagement strategies. 
  • Develop and lead integrated communications strategies that strengthen member understanding, connection and engagement with the organization. 
  • Build communications plans around major organizational initiatives, changes, announcements and priorities. 
  • Play a lead role in building a monthly membership newsletter. 
  • Establish meaningful measures of communications and member engagement effectiveness. 

Requirements


Minimum Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in corporate communications, media relations, membership communications or a related field, ideally within sports, entertainment, or nonprofit sectors.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Communications, Journalism, Marketing, Public Relations, or a related field; advanced degree a plus. 
  • Strong understanding of the U.S. soccer ecosystem, including key stakeholders such as members, referees, coaches, and youth programs. 
  • Proven experience supporting C-suite executives with briefing materials, talking points, presentations, and internal/external messaging. 
  • Exceptional writing, editing, and verbal communication skills across a variety of formats (speeches, memos, newsletters, social content, feature articles, etc.). 
  • Demonstrated ability to manage sensitive information and craft strategic responses in high-pressure or time-sensitive situations. 
  • Experience coordinating communications for high-profile events, such as board meetings, conventions, and internal town halls. 
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to balance multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Ability to develop clear, consistent messaging across internal and external channels, aligned with organizational mission and voice. 
  • Comfort working collaboratively across departments and building relationships at all levels of an organization. 
  • Experience communicating with a membership, association, nonprofit or similarly diverse stakeholder base strongly preferred.
  • General knowledge of soccer.
  • Capable of working in fast-paced and demanding environments.
  • Must be able to connect “micro” details to the “macro” vision and mission.
  • Ability to work flexible hours, including evenings, weekends, and travel up to two times per quarter. 
  • Proficient experience with Microsoft Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook). 

Desired Qualifications 

  • Strategic hustle, initiative, and work ethic with diversity of thought. 
  • Strong posture for empathy. 
  • Ability to build meaningful relationships both internally and externally. 
  • Able to think strategically and handle multiple projects. 
  • Confidence without ego. 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
  • Spanish language proficiency is a plus, but not required. 

 

U.S. Soccer offers a comprehensive compensation package, casual work environment, an inclusive culture, and an atmosphere for professional development.


U.S. Soccer is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion, and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, citizenship, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, military status, political belief, or any other characteristic protected under the law. This policy applies to all our employment practices within our organization. We strongly encourage women, people of color, LGBTQIA, veterans, parents, and persons with disabilities to apply.

This is an exciting opportunity to deliver on our Football Development activities at one or more of our locations: Wolverhampton, Telford, Shrewsbury, Codsall, Newport, Cannock or Stafford and to support the international programme.

This role involves coaching across the Football Development programme and working with other staff to deliver high-quality sessions updating player tracking and liaising with full-time staff on the evaluation of players.

Please note that this is a casual role.

For more details on this role and the requirements, please see the job description.

Ref - JH-025-23082024

job.title: Host Families Required
job.html_description:
Host Families Required

Wolves are seeking host families who can provide accommodation for Academy players aged 14-19 years. Our ideal Host family provision will be able to offer our young players a stable, safe and comfortable environment. We believe our players perform better on the pitch when they are settled and content at home.

At Wolves we pride ourselves on a nurturing environment and we want our players to fulfil their potential both ON and OFF the pitch.

For more details on how to register your interest in becoming a host family, please see the Host Families Description below.

All queries and applications should be directed to hostfamily@wolves.co.uk

An exciting opportunity has arisen to work within our Football Development department as an International Development Coach.

The successful candidate will be responsible for leading and delivering a high-quality college programme with a partnered international school, working primarily on Mondays and Tuesdays in Hereford. 

The role will also focus on development of football players in this international school, delivering high level technical and tactical sessions.

Please note that this is a casual role.

job.title: Security Officer - Part Time
job.html_description:
Security Officer - Part Time

An exciting opportunity has arisen to work within our Security Team as a Security Officer.

The successful candidate will be required to maintain a safe & secure environment, acting as a visual deterrent, prevent loss prevention, completing reports & company documentation whilst providing a professional, responsive & observant security presence.

This is a part-time position, working an average of 30.25 hours per week on a rolling 2 week shift pattern as follows:

Week 1

  1. Monday: 1:00am – 9:00am (7.5 hours)
  2. Tuesday: 1:00am – 9:00am (7.5 hours)
  3. Saturday: 9:00pm – 9:00am (11.5 hours)
  4. Sunday: 9:00pm – 9:00am (11.5 hours)

Week 2

  1. Wednesday: 1:00am – 9:00am (7.5 hours)
  2. Thursday: 1:00am – 9:00am (7.5 hours)
  3. Friday: 1:00am – 9:00am (7.5 hours)

For details on the role and its requirements, please see the below job description.

Ref: RB-00-01072026

Closing date: 29th September 2026

JOB DESCRIPTION

job.title: Turnstile Operator (Casual)
job.html_description:
Turnstile Operator (Casual)

To admit spectators, check tickets.

Turnstile operators are not expected to be involved with searching or ejecting spectators or dealing with conflict. Their role is specific, and they will be expected to call on a supervisor or specialist stewards for assistance in dealing with any incident at their turnstile.

Turnstile Operators are supported by search stewards and a supervisor. 

For more details on this role and the requirements, please see the below job description.

Ref: AR-296-06072022 

JOB DESCRIPTION
